laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Amendment 64 (21+, 1 oz / 3 oz home)
laws.subtitle: C.R.S. 18-18-406 — Licensed dispensaries only
laws.fullDescription: Colorado was the first state to legalize recreational cannabis in 2012 (Amendment 64). Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz in public and 3 oz at home. Up to 3 plants may be grown at home (6 per household). Must purchase from licensed dispensaries. Public consumption (parks, streets, concerts) is illegal — $100 fine.
laws.penalty: Public consumption: $100 fine. Driving under influence: DUI charges, same as alcohol. Selling without license: criminal charges.
exceptions: Private property with owner's permission only for consumption
Denver has an 'opt-in' licensed hospitality consumption program for some businesses

quiz.q: Maximum cannabis plants allowed per household in Colorado?
quiz.explanation: Colorado allows up to 6 cannabis plants per household (for adults 21+) for personal cultivation under Amendment 64.

laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law — HB 1035 (2023)
laws.subtitle: Colorado distracted driving — $65 first offense
laws.fullDescription: Colorado passed HB 1035 in 2023 requiring hands-free use of mobile devices while driving. Cannot hold or use a handheld device. Fines increase with repeat offenses. Applies even at traffic lights.
laws.penalty: 1st offense: $65 + 2 points. 2nd within 3 years: $150 + 2 points. 3rd+: $250 + 4 points.
exceptions: Emergency 911 calls
Law enforcement
Parked completely off roadway

quiz.q: Colorado first-offense fine for hands-free violation (2023 law)?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's 2023 HB 1035 sets a $65 fine for a first handheld device violation while driving.

laws.title: Colorado Outdoor Culture — Leave No Trace & High-Altitude Respect
laws.subtitle: 'LNT' ethics, altitude sickness awareness, dog friendliness
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's culture revolves around the outdoors. 'Leave No Trace' (LNT) principles are widely known and respected — pack out all trash, stay on trails, don't disturb wildlife. At altitude (above 8,000 ft), be aware of altitude sickness: hydrate, ascend slowly, recognize symptoms. Dogs are everywhere — Colorado is extremely dog-friendly. Skiing etiquette on slopes: yield to those below you, be aware of speed.
laws.penalty: No legal penalty — but violating Leave No Trace ethics in wilderness areas may violate federal regulations.
exceptions: Front Range cities (Denver, Boulder, Fort Collins) have a more urban cafe culture alongside outdoor focus
Eastern Colorado is more agricultural and traditional
laws.sourceLabel: Leave No Trace Center for Outdoor Ethics

quiz.q: According to Leave No Trace ethics, what must you always do with your trash in Colorado's wilderness?
options: Leave it in a pile for rangers
quiz.explanation: Leave No Trace ethics require you to 'pack it out' — all trash must be carried out of wilderness areas, leaving no trace of your visit.

laws.title: 14er Hiking Safety Laws — Altitude and Rescue Liability
laws.subtitle: Colorado SAR — False distress calls: $300+ fine; altitude: life-threatening
laws.fullDescription: Colorado has 58 peaks above 14,000 feet ('14ers'). Altitude sickness is a genuine medical risk above 8,000 feet — headache, nausea, and fatigue are warning signs; pulmonary oedema above 12,000 feet can be fatal. Colorado's search and rescue (SAR) is largely volunteer-funded. Making a false distress call or activating an emergency beacon negligently can result in billing for rescue costs (increasingly common) and criminal charges. Many 14ers require early starts (before noon) to avoid afternoon lightning storms — a leading cause of death on Colorado mountains.
laws.penalty: False distress call: misdemeanour + fine. Negligent beacon activation: cost recovery. Failure to register in some areas when required: warning.
exceptions: Genuine emergencies are never penalised
Proper pre-registration reduces SAR burden
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Search and Rescue Fund / Colorado Statute §33-32-107

quiz.q: Why do experienced hikers aim to summit Colorado 14ers before noon?
options: To avoid dangerous afternoon lightning storms
quiz.explanation: Afternoon lightning storms are a leading cause of death on Colorado's 14ers — experienced hikers aim to summit by noon and descend before the storms typically build around 1–3pm.

laws.title: Wolf Reintroduction — Colorado Proposition 114
laws.subtitle: Prop 114 (2020) — Gray wolves reintroduced December 2023
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters narrowly passed Proposition 114 in 2020, mandating the reintroduction of gray wolves to Colorado by the end of 2023. In December 2023, 10 gray wolves were relocated from Oregon to Colorado's Western Slope. Under federal and state law, gray wolves are a protected species — killing, injuring, or harassing a gray wolf is illegal and carries significant federal penalties. Ranchers with livestock losses from wolf attacks may apply for government compensation. The reintroduction is contentious among ranchers, farmers, and rural communities.
laws.penalty: Killing a protected gray wolf: federal felony under the Endangered Species Act — up to $50,000 fine + 1 year imprisonment.
exceptions: Immediate self-defence from a direct wolf attack (very narrow)
Authorised wildlife management actions by CDPHE
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Parks and Wildlife — Wolf Restoration

quiz.q: When were gray wolves reintroduced to Colorado under Proposition 114?
quiz.explanation: Colorado voters approved wolf reintroduction in 2020, and the first 10 gray wolves were relocated from Oregon to Colorado's Western Slope in December 2023.

laws.title: Colorado Public Lands Access — Trespass and Trail Rules
laws.subtitle: Colorado Open Range Law — Cattle right-of-way; trespass protections
laws.fullDescription: Colorado has an 'Open Range' tradition — livestock may legally roam on unfenced public land and even across roads. Drivers who hit cattle on an open range road may be liable (not the rancher). Trespassing on private land in Colorado (even through scenic mountains) is a criminal offence — many scenic areas in the Rockies are private, and people frequently trespass assuming public access. The Colorado Trail and other federal trails are public but surrounding land may be private. Camping on private land without permission is trespass. Colorado has a 'No Hunting Without Permission' law for all private land regardless of whether it's fenced.
laws.penalty: Criminal trespass: Class 2 misdemeanor — up to 120 days jail + $750 fine. Hunting on private land without permission: Class 2 misdemeanor + licence revocation.
exceptions: Federal and state public lands — trails like the Colorado Trail are public
Emergency situations — injured person may cross private land for help

quiz.q: Under Colorado's Open Range law, who may be liable if a car hits cattle on an unfenced road?
options: The driver — ranchers are not required to fence cattle off public roads
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Open Range law means cattle can legally be on unfenced roads — if a driver hits them, the driver (not the rancher) may bear liability since the rancher has no legal duty to fence the road.

laws.title: Ski Resort Responsibility Code — Colorado's Skier Safety Act
laws.subtitle: C.R.S. §33-44 — Skiers assume inherent risks; collisions and recklessness are illegal
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Ski Safety Act (CRS §33-44) governs conduct on ski slopes. The Skier Responsibility Code is legally binding: always yield to those below you, always look uphill before merging, stop only at the side of a run, and never ski faster than your ability allows. Reckless skiing that causes injury to another person can result in criminal charges — reckless endangerment in Colorado is a class 3 misdemeanor. Ski resorts are also required by law to have marked ski patrols, clearly posted trail difficulty ratings, and rescue access routes. Skiing off-piste into closed areas is a serious violation that can result in being banned from the resort and billed for rescue costs.
laws.penalty: Reckless skiing causing injury: class 3 misdemeanor (up to 6 months + $750 fine). Ski resort bill for rescue in closed area: $1,000–$5,000+.
exceptions: Patrol-approved backcountry access zones with proper avalanche equipment
Competition events with safety officers and cleared courses
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Revised Statutes §33-44 — Ski Safety Act

quiz.q: Under Colorado's Skier Responsibility Code, who must yield to whom?
options: Faster skiers have right of way
Skiers above must yield to those below
Skiers below must yield to those coming from above
Both skiers must negotiate right of way
quiz.explanation: The fundamental rule of skiing: the skier above must yield to those below — because the downhill skier cannot see what's coming from behind.

laws.title: Colorado Recreational Cannabis — Legal but Restricted; Public Use Banned
laws.subtitle: Amendment 64 (2012) — 1oz possession; no smoking in public; 25mg edible limit
laws.fullDescription: Colorado was the first US state to legalise recreational cannabis in 2012 (Amendment 64). Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 ounce (28g) of cannabis, purchase from licensed dispensaries, and grow up to 3 mature plants at home. However, public consumption is illegal — the same smoking restrictions as tobacco apply, plus cannabis may not be used in vehicles or on federal land (national parks, national forests). Colorado's edible cannabis regulations are strict: individual servings must be clearly dosed at 10mg THC or less, and packaging must be child-resistant and not resemble candy. Driving under the influence of cannabis is a criminal offence (5 nanograms THC per millilitre of blood is the limit, though impairment can occur below this).
laws.penalty: Public cannabis consumption: $100 fine. Cannabis DUI: criminal charge + licence suspension. Selling to under-21: Class 1 misdemeanor.
exceptions: Licensed cannabis consumption lounges in certain municipalities
Private residences where owner permits use

quiz.q: What was the maximum THC blood concentration used for Colorado cannabis DUI enforcement?
options: No legal limit — only impairment tested
quiz.explanation: Colorado uses 5 nanograms of THC per millilitre of blood as a threshold for cannabis DUI — though unlike alcohol, this is a rebuttable presumption of impairment rather than an absolute limit, as THC metabolism varies widely.

laws.title: Fourteener Trail Regulations — Leave No Trace Mandatory
laws.subtitle: Colorado's 14,000-foot peaks have strict access and trail ethics rules
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's 58 'fourteeners' (peaks exceeding 14,000 feet) attract over 500,000 annual climbers, creating significant environmental pressure. The Colorado Fourteener Initiative and state regulations require strict Leave No Trace practices: packing out all waste, staying on designated trails, camping 200+ feet from water sources, and using established toilets or WAG bags above treeline. Several popular peaks like Grays Peak and Mount Democrat have seasonal wildlife closures for ptarmigan nesting. Dogs must be leashed on many fourteeners during summer. Drones are banned in wilderness areas. Camping fires above treeline are prohibited year-round.
laws.penalty: Trail violations: fines $50–$500. Wilderness rule violations: fines up to $5,000. Drone violations: $1,000+ per FAA and wilderness regulations.
exceptions: Authorized scientific research with permits
Search and rescue operations
Established pack animals with grazing permits

quiz.q: What practice is required when climbing Colorado fourteeners above treeline?
options: Pack out all waste using WAG bags
Register at ranger stations each day
quiz.explanation: Above treeline on Colorado fourteeners, climbers must pack out all human waste using WAG (Waste Alleviation and Gelling) bags, as there is no soil for decomposition at high altitudes.

laws.title: Colorado Amendment 64 — First US State to Fully Legalize Recreational Cannabis (2012)
laws.subtitle: Colorado and Washington pioneered legal cannabis in 2012; Colorado retail sales model became template
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Amendment 64 (November 2012) made it the first US state (with Washington) to legalize recreational cannabis for adults 21+. The Colorado Retail Marijuana Code established a state-licensed retail system: licensed dispensaries, tested products, child-proof packaging, and warning labels. Adults may possess up to 1 ounce (28g) in public; home cultivation of up to 6 plants is legal. Out-of-state visitors can purchase but cannot carry across state lines (still federal crime). Colorado collected over $1.7 billion in cannabis tax revenue from 2014–2022. Social equity provisions were added in 2020 to address disparate enforcement histories. Colorado's system (with its regulatory framework, tested products, and age verification) became the model adopted by most subsequent states. Federal law still classifies cannabis as Schedule I.
laws.penalty: Possession over 1oz: misdemeanor + fine. Public consumption in non-permitted areas: $100 fine. Selling to minors: felony (2–6 years imprisonment). Driving under influence: DUI laws apply.
exceptions: Medical marijuana patients have higher possession limits
Home cultivation up to 6 plants per adult (max 12 per household) is legal
Consumption lounges licensed since 2020 allow on-site use
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division — Retail Rules

quiz.q: How much tax revenue did Colorado collect from cannabis sales from 2014 to 2022?
quiz.explanation: Colorado collected over $1.7 billion in cannabis tax revenue from the launch of retail sales in 2014 through 2022 — funds that went primarily to public school construction, law enforcement, and public health programs, demonstrating the fiscal benefits that other states cited when considering legalization.

laws.title: Colorado's TABOR Amendment — Unique Voter Approval Required for Tax Increases
laws.subtitle: Colorado's 1992 Taxpayer's Bill of Rights requires voter approval for all tax increases and spending limits
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Taxpayer's Bill of Rights (TABOR, Article X, Section 20 of the Colorado Constitution, adopted 1992) is one of the nation's most restrictive fiscal constraints. It requires voter approval for all tax rate increases, new taxes, and any government revenue above a cap based on inflation plus population growth. Excess revenues must be refunded to taxpayers ('TABOR refunds'). The amendment has been both praised (limiting government growth) and criticized (creating fiscal crises — Colorado voters repeatedly waive TABOR limits through 'de-Brucing' mechanisms). When cannabis was legalized (2012), TABOR required a separate vote to keep cannabis tax revenues (voters approved Proposition AA). Every significant government revenue decision requires a ballot measure — creating a uniquely direct democracy approach to fiscal policy.
laws.penalty: Government collecting taxes beyond TABOR limits without voter approval: mandatory refunds to taxpayers. Violations subject to legal challenge and court-ordered reimbursement.
exceptions: Federal grants and pass-through funds are not subject to TABOR
Revenue from enterprise funds (user fees, not taxes) is exempt
Emergency spending following disaster declarations has modified requirements

quiz.q: What does Colorado's TABOR amendment require when the government's revenue exceeds the cap set by inflation plus population growth?
options: The excess must be deposited in a rainy day fund
The excess must be refunded to taxpayers
The excess may be spent on infrastructure without a vote
The Governor may allocate the excess with legislative approval
quiz.explanation: Colorado's TABOR amendment requires that excess revenues above the inflation-plus-population-growth cap must be refunded to taxpayers — these 'TABOR refunds' have been issued multiple times, most recently in 2021–2023 when Colorado's strong economy generated large surpluses that had to be returned to residents as checks.

laws.title: TABOR — Taxpayer Bill of Rights
laws.subtitle: Colorado's unique constitutional amendment caps government spending and requires voter approval for tax increases
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Taxpayer Bill of Rights (TABOR), passed by voters in 1992, is a constitutional amendment requiring voter approval for any tax rate increase, limiting government revenue growth to inflation plus population growth, and mandating refunds of excess tax revenue. TABOR is unique in American governance — no other state has adopted an equivalent. Critics argue it has created a fiscal straitjacket: Colorado ranked near bottom for per-pupil school funding for years; roads, hospitals, and public services were chronically underfunded. Supporters call it a model for fiscal restraint. The state has periodically suspended parts of TABOR via voter-approved measures like Referendum C (2005).
laws.penalty: Government agencies that retain excess revenue above TABOR limits without voter approval face constitutional violations. Citizens can sue the state to recover overcharged taxes.
exceptions: Voters can temporarily suspend TABOR revenue limits through ballot measures
Federal funds are not subject to TABOR limits
Enterprise funds (fee-based government businesses) are exempt from TABOR
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Office of State Planning and Budgeting — TABOR

quiz.q: What does Colorado's TABOR require the government to do with tax revenue collected above the constitutional limit?
options: Invest it in a sovereign wealth fund
Put it to a public vote for allocation
quiz.explanation: Colorado's TABOR requires the government to refund excess tax revenue above the constitutional growth limit to taxpayers — a provision unique to Colorado that has resulted in hundreds of millions of dollars in refund checks to residents.

laws.title: Amendment 64 — First Legal Recreational Cannabis Market
laws.subtitle: Colorado and Washington became the first US states to legalize recreational cannabis in 2012
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Amendment 64 (passed November 2012, effective January 1, 2014) made Colorado the world's first jurisdiction to create a fully regulated recreational cannabis market open to adults 21+. (Washington State passed a similar initiative simultaneously.) The Colorado model — with licensed dispensaries, potency testing, child-resistant packaging, seed-to-sale tracking, and excise taxes — became the global template. By 2023, Colorado had generated over $1.8 billion in cannabis tax revenue; over $200 million was earmarked for public school construction. Over 30 US states followed with legal cannabis programs. Colorado also pioneered the 'cannabis equity' concept — programs to help communities disproportionately harmed by drug prohibition enter the legal market.
laws.penalty: Sales to under-21s: up to $100,000 fine and license revocation. Unlicensed sales: up to $100,000 fine and 18 months imprisonment. Driving under the influence of cannabis (5ng THC blood limit): same penalties as alcohol DUI.
exceptions: Medical marijuana patients may purchase higher quantities
Home cultivation of up to 6 plants per adult (max 12 per household) is legal
Cannabis cafes (consumption lounges) are permitted with separate licensing
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Department of Revenue — Marijuana Enforcement

quiz.q: How much cannabis tax revenue had Colorado generated by 2023 since legalizing recreational cannabis in 2014?
quiz.explanation: Colorado generated over $1.8 billion in cannabis tax revenue in the decade since legalizing recreational cannabis in 2014 — with over $200 million earmarked for public school construction, making it a model for other states considering legalization.

laws.title: TABOR: Colorado's Taxpayer's Bill of Rights
laws.subtitle: Colorado's 1992 constitutional amendment requires voter approval for all tax increases and refunds excess revenue — uniquely limiting government growth
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Taxpayer's Bill of Rights (TABOR), passed by voter initiative in 1992, is embedded in the state constitution and requires that all tax rate increases be approved by voters, limits state spending growth to inflation plus population growth, and mandates that excess revenue be refunded to taxpayers. It is unique in US law — no other state has such strict constitutional limits on government revenue. TABOR has resulted in hundreds of millions in taxpayer refunds in boom years but has also led to significant underfunding of schools, transportation, and healthcare during lean years. Colorado voters have periodically 'de-Bruced' (suspended TABOR limits) for specific purposes but the underlying amendment remains.
laws.penalty: Government officials who violate TABOR requirements (collecting excess taxes without voter approval) face personal liability and mandatory refunds. Courts have enforced TABOR through injunctions
exceptions: Enterprises' revenues (like CDOT toll roads) are excluded from TABOR limits
Voters can approve temporary suspension of TABOR limits for specific programs through ballot initiatives
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Office of Legislative Legal Services – TABOR

quiz.q: What does Colorado's TABOR amendment require before the state can raise taxes?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's TABOR (Taxpayer's Bill of Rights) requires voter approval for all state and local tax rate increases — a unique constitutional constraint that no other US state has in such comprehensive form.

laws.title: Proposition 122: Colorado Legalizes Psilocybin Therapy & Natural Medicines
laws.subtitle: Colorado became the second US state to legalize psilocybin mushrooms — and went further by creating a regulated healing center framework
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Proposition 122, passed in November 2022, decriminalized personal possession and home growing of psilocybin mushrooms, psilocin, ibogaine, DMT, and mescaline (from non-peyote sources) for adults 21+, and created a regulated 'natural medicine' healing center framework similar to Oregon's Measure 109. Licensed facilitators can offer supervised psilocybin sessions at healing centers. Colorado went beyond Oregon's model by including ibogaine (used for opioid addiction treatment) and allowing social sharing. The state began issuing healing center licenses in 2024. Federal law still classifies psilocybin as Schedule I, but federal enforcement of state-legal activities has been minimal.
laws.penalty: Possession within personal limits: no penalty (decriminalized). Selling outside the licensed framework: criminal drug trafficking charges still apply. Operating a healing center without a license: civil and criminal penalties
exceptions: Ibogaine is included despite being Schedule I federally — unique among US state laws
Gifting (social sharing without payment) of natural medicines between adults is permitted
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Dept. of Public Health & Environment – Natural Medicine

quiz.q: What makes Colorado's Proposition 122 broader than Oregon's psilocybin law?
options: Colorado allows retail sales without a facilitator
Colorado includes additional substances like ibogaine and DMT, and allows social sharing
Colorado allows home delivery of psilocybin
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Prop 122 goes beyond Oregon's model by including ibogaine, DMT, and mescaline alongside psilocybin, and permitting social sharing (gifting) between adults — making it the broadest psychedelic reform law in the US.

laws.title: FAMLI Paid Leave
laws.subtitle: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance program — mandatory paid leave
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Act, passed by voters in 2020 and effective from 2024, requires all employers to participate in a state-run paid leave insurance program. Employees can take up to 12 weeks of paid leave (16 weeks for pregnancy-related conditions) for serious medical conditions, caring for a family member, military leave, or safe leave (domestic violence). Benefits replace up to 90% of wages for low-income workers. Premiums are split between employers and employees. Colorado joins a small number of US states with comprehensive paid family leave, as there is no federal equivalent.
laws.penalty: Employers who fail to remit premiums face fines; retaliation against employees for taking leave is prohibited with civil remedies
exceptions: Employers with fewer than 10 employees don't pay the employer portion of premiums
Self-employed workers may opt in voluntarily

quiz.q: How many weeks of paid leave does Colorado's FAMLI provide for pregnancy-related conditions?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's FAMLI Act provides up to 12 weeks of paid leave for most qualifying reasons, and up to 16 weeks for pregnancy-related conditions.

laws.title: Wolf Reintroduction Law
laws.subtitle: Colorado voters approved gray wolf reintroduction in 2020
laws.fullDescription: Colorado Proposition 114 (2020) — approved by voters 50.9% to 49.1% — mandated that Colorado Parks and Wildlife reintroduce gray wolves to the state by the end of 2023. Colorado became the first state to restore wolves through a citizen vote rather than a federal or state agency decision. In December 2023, the first wolves from Oregon were released in Grand County. Ranchers who lose livestock to wolf predation can receive compensation from a dedicated fund. The reintroduction is controversial among ranchers and rural communities but supported by wildlife advocates who argue wolves are a keystone species that restores ecosystem balance.
laws.penalty: Killing a wolf: federal Endangered Species Act violation — fines up to $50,000 and up to 1 year imprisonment; lethal removal only by CPW in specific circumstances
exceptions: Wolves that directly threaten human safety can be removed by wildlife officials
Livestock owners have provisions for non-lethal deterrence reimbursement

quiz.q: By what margin did Colorado voters approve wolf reintroduction in 2020?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Proposition 114 passed by the narrowest possible margin — 50.9% to 49.1% — reflecting deep divisions between urban voters (who supported reintroduction) and rural ranching communities (who largely opposed it).

laws.title: Ski Resort Liability Law
laws.subtitle: Colorado's ski law limits liability for injuries on slopes but requires helmets for minors
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Ski Safety Act (1979, amended) establishes a shared responsibility framework for ski area injuries. Skiers and snowboarders assume the 'inherent risks of skiing' — falls, variable conditions, collisions with natural features — and cannot sue ski areas for these. However, ski areas remain liable for artificial hazards they negligently create or fail to warn about. Colorado's ski helmet law requires children under 18 to wear helmets when skiing or snowboarding. Colorado has the most ski resorts of any US state (approximately 30), and Vail Mountain alone attracts 1.5 million skier visits annually.
laws.penalty: Ski area operators who create unreasonable hazards: civil liability; violating helmet law for minors: parental fine of $20; ski jumping or terrain park operators have heightened duties of care
exceptions: Race and training areas have different standards as participants assume higher risk
Backcountry and off-piste skiing is not regulated by the Ski Safety Act

quiz.q: What does Colorado's Ski Safety Act say about 'inherent risks of skiing'?
options: Skiers can sue for any injury
Ski areas must compensate all injuries
Skiers assume inherent risks like falls and collisions with natural features
Ski areas are automatically liable for all accidents
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Ski Safety Act establishes that skiers assume the 'inherent risks of skiing' — meaning ski areas are not liable for injuries from falls, variable snow conditions, or collisions with natural features. Areas remain liable only for negligently created artificial hazards.

laws.title: Natural Medicine Health Act (Proposition 122)
laws.subtitle: Colorado's 2022 law decriminalized psilocybin and other psychedelic plants for therapeutic use
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters approved Proposition 122 (the Natural Medicine Health Act) in November 2022 by 53.4%, making Colorado the second state after Oregon (2020) to decriminalize psilocybin (magic mushrooms) and the first to also decriminalize other natural psychedelics including psilocin, dimethyltryptamine (DMT), ibogaine, and mescaline (not from peyote). The law created a regulated system for 'natural medicine healing centers' where adults 21+ can receive supervised psychedelic therapy. Personal possession, use, and home cultivation of small amounts was decriminalized. The Colorado Behavioral Health Administration is developing regulations for the healing center program. Research suggests psychedelics may be effective for treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, and addiction. The law does not allow retail sale for unsupervised home use; all therapeutic use must occur in supervised facilities.
laws.penalty: Selling natural medicines outside licensed healing centers remains illegal; possession over personal use limits: misdemeanor; driving under influence: DUI penalties
exceptions: Supervised therapeutic use in licensed healing centers is fully legal
Personal possession and home cultivation of small amounts is decriminalized (not criminal)
Religious ceremonial use (e.g., Native American Church peyote use) is separately protected under federal law

laws.title: Colorado's Election Security and Vote-by-Mail Model
laws.subtitle: Colorado's universal vote-by-mail system with paper ballots is considered the gold standard for election security
laws.fullDescription: Colorado has been a leader in election security and access since moving to universal mail-in voting in 2013 (HB 13-1303) and implementing comprehensive security measures thereafter. Colorado's election law framework includes: all registered voters automatically receive a mail ballot; voters can also vote in-person at Voter Service and Polling Centers; every ballot has a unique barcode trackable by voters; ballots are printed on high-security paper; all voting systems must have paper audit trails; post-election risk-limiting audits are mandatory (first state to codify this requirement in law); voter rolls use the Electronic Registration Information Center (ERIC) for cross-state database matching; and a bipartisan team of county clerks must observe tabulation. Colorado's Secure Ballot Initiative and the County Clerks and Recorders Association have both been cited as models nationally and internationally. Despite this, Colorado faced disinformation campaigns questioning its election integrity.
laws.penalty: Election fraud: felony charges (1-6 years imprisonment); election interference by officials: criminal and civil liability; violating ballot secrecy: misdemeanor
exceptions: Overseas and military voters have extended deadlines
Voters who miss the mail ballot deadline may vote provisionally in person
Election observers from all parties have legal access to all stages of the process

laws.title: FAMLI Act – Paid Family and Medical Leave
laws.subtitle: Colorado launched a state-run paid leave program funded by payroll contributions
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters approved Proposition 118 in 2020, creating the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) program — one of the most comprehensive paid leave laws in the US. Starting in 2024, eligible employees can receive up to 12 weeks (up to 16 for qualifying pregnancy-related conditions) of paid leave at 90% of wages (capped at 90% of state average weekly wage). The program is funded by 0.9% payroll contributions split between employers and employees. Colorado joins a small number of states — including California, New York, and Washington — with comprehensive paid family leave. Self-employed workers may opt in.
laws.penalty: Employer interference with FAMLI rights: civil penalties up to $500/day per violation. Retaliation against employees using FAMLI: additional fines and reinstatement orders.
exceptions: Employers with fewer than 10 employees pay only the employee's portion
Employers with equivalent or better private insurance plans may apply for approval to substitute
Federal employees are excluded (covered by separate federal law)

quiz.q: How is Colorado's FAMLI paid leave program funded?
options: 0.9% payroll contribution split between employer and employee
quiz.explanation: FAMLI is funded by a 0.9% payroll contribution split between employers and employees, with employers covering half and deducting the employee's share from paychecks.

laws.title: Proposition 122 – Colorado Legalizes Psychedelic Therapy
laws.subtitle: Colorado became the second US state to decriminalize and regulate natural psychedelics
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters approved Proposition 122 in November 2022, decriminalizing personal use, possession, and home cultivation of psilocybin (magic mushrooms), psilocin, DMT, ibogaine, and mescaline for adults 21+. It also created a regulated 'healing center' model for supervised therapeutic use — the Natural Medicine Health Act. Colorado followed Oregon (2020) in this approach. The first licensed healing centers began operating in 2024. The law reflects growing scientific evidence that psychedelic-assisted therapy may treat depression, PTSD, addiction, and end-of-life anxiety. Critics raised concerns about misuse and lack of long-term safety data. Federal law still classifies these substances as Schedule I controlled substances.
laws.penalty: Sharing or providing natural psychedelics without compensation: not criminal (decriminalized). Selling outside licensed healing centers: still criminal — up to 2 years imprisonment.
exceptions: Personal home cultivation for personal use is decriminalized (not fully legal)
Licensed healing centers operate under strict regulatory framework
Driving under influence of psychedelics: DUI laws fully apply

quiz.q: Which psychedelic substances did Colorado's Proposition 122 decriminalize for personal use?
options: Psilocybin, psilocin, DMT, ibogaine, and mescaline
All Schedule I and II controlled substances
LSD and MDMA in addition to natural psychedelics
quiz.explanation: Proposition 122 decriminalized personal use and home cultivation of five natural psychedelics: psilocybin, psilocin, DMT, ibogaine, and mescaline — while creating a regulated healing center model for supervised therapeutic use.

laws.title: Colorado River Crisis and Water Rights Renegotiation
laws.subtitle: The Colorado River's historic decline forced seven states to renegotiate water allocations
laws.fullDescription: The Colorado River, which supplies water to 40 million people and 5.5 million acres of farmland, reached historic low levels — Lake Mead (the largest US reservoir) dropped to 27% capacity by 2022. The Bureau of Reclamation threatened mandatory cuts under the 1922 Colorado River Compact if states didn't voluntarily reduce use. Colorado, as an upper basin state, participated in multi-state negotiations under the 2026 interim guidelines process. The 2023 'Supplemental Environmental Impact Statement' proposed 1.5-3.5 million acre-feet cuts. Agriculture uses ~80% of river water, making farmland fallowing the primary conservation mechanism. Climate change projections suggest the river will carry 10-30% less water by mid-century.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized water diversion above junior water rights priority: state water court enforcement and required curtailment. Federal compact violation: federal court action against states.
exceptions: Tribal water rights (senior to 1922 compact) protected and being formalized through settlement negotiations
Prior appropriation doctrine protects senior water rights holders from junior curtailment

quiz.q: To what capacity did Lake Mead fall by 2022, triggering mandatory water cut negotiations?
quiz.explanation: Lake Mead — the Colorado River's largest reservoir — fell to approximately 27% of capacity by 2022 (its lowest since it first filled in the 1930s), triggering federal threats of mandatory cuts under the Colorado River Compact and multi-state emergency negotiations.

laws.title: Colorado's AI Consumer Protection Act
laws.subtitle: First US state law requiring AI risk assessments for high-risk deployments
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 205, 2024) became the first comprehensive US state AI law requiring companies that deploy 'high-risk artificial intelligence systems' in consequential decisions (employment, education, healthcare, housing, financial services) to conduct annual risk assessments and protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination. Deployers must notify individuals when AI is used in consequential decisions and provide a right to appeal. The Colorado attorney general can enforce the law. The law mirrors aspects of the EU AI Act but was opposed by some AI companies and the Colorado governor requested amendments before signing.
laws.penalty: Violations of AI Act requirements: Colorado AG can seek civil penalties. Failure to conduct required risk assessments: injunctions and remediation orders. Discriminatory AI deployment: violations of existing anti-discrimination law in addition to AI Act penalties
exceptions: AI systems used by small businesses with limited risk may qualify for exemptions
AI used for national security purposes is excluded
Open-source AI developers have modified requirements depending on deployment context

quiz.q: What was historically significant about Colorado's Artificial Intelligence Act (2024)?
options: First law to ban AI entirely
First comprehensive US state law requiring AI risk assessments for high-risk systems
First law to regulate AI on the federal level
First law requiring AI to be human-supervised
quiz.explanation: Colorado's SB 205 became the first comprehensive US state law requiring companies deploying 'high-risk' AI in consequential decisions to conduct annual risk assessments and protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.

laws.title: Colorado's Magic Mushroom Regulation
laws.subtitle: Colorado became second state to decriminalize and regulate psilocybin
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters passed Proposition 122 in November 2022, making Colorado the second US state (after Oregon) to decriminalize and create a regulated access system for psilocybin mushrooms and other natural psychedelics (including DMT, ibogaine, and mescaline). Adults 21+ can possess, grow, and use psilocybin without criminal penalty. A licensed 'healing center' system allows supervised therapeutic use. The Proposition also created the Natural Medicine Advisory Board. Colorado's natural medicine services program began in 2024. Personal cultivation for home use was immediately decriminalized; the full licensing system rolled out more slowly.
laws.penalty: Selling psilocybin outside licensed system: criminal prosecution. Giving psilocybin to minors: felony. Operating unlicensed healing center: criminal prosecution. Personal possession/cultivation within legal limits: not a crime
exceptions: Licensed healing centers can charge for supervised psilocybin sessions
Persons in clinical trials are not covered by the same rules
Indigenous and religious ceremonial use has some protected status in practice
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment - Natural Medicine

quiz.q: Besides psilocybin, what other natural psychedelics did Colorado's Proposition 122 decriminalize?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Proposition 122 decriminalized not just psilocybin but also DMT (found in ayahuasca), ibogaine (used for addiction treatment), and mescaline (found in peyote) — making it broader than Oregon's psilocybin-only measure.

laws.title: FAMLI Paid Family Leave Law
laws.subtitle: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance program began in 2024
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) program, approved by voters in 2020 and launched in 2024, provides workers up to 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave annually. Employees can take leave for birth/adoption, serious personal health conditions, caring for ill family members, or safety needs related to domestic violence. Both employees and employers contribute premiums. Employers with 10+ employees must contribute; small employers contribute less. Interference with FAMLI rights or retaliation against employees who use FAMLI is illegal. Private employers must post FAMLI notices.
laws.penalty: Employer interference with FAMLI rights: civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation; retaliation: reinstatement and back pay
exceptions: Federal employees covered by separate federal leave laws
Certain railroad workers under federal statutes

quiz.q: When did Colorado's FAMLI paid leave program launch for benefits?
quiz.explanation: Although Colorado voters approved FAMLI in 2020, the program launched actual benefits payments in January 2024.

laws.title: Colorado Privacy Act and Data Rights
laws.subtitle: Colorado's CPA grants consumers data rights similar to GDPR
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Privacy Act (CPA), effective July 2023, created consumer rights to access, correct, delete, and opt out of the processing of personal data. Businesses must conduct data protection assessments for high-risk processing. Consumers can opt out of targeted advertising, sale of personal data, and profiling. Unlike some state privacy laws, Colorado's CPA applies to nonprofit organizations. The Attorney General and district attorneys can enforce the law with fines up to $20,000 per violation. Colorado's law is considered one of the stronger US state privacy statutes, along with Virginia, California, and Connecticut laws.
laws.penalty: Violations after cure period: fines up to $20,000 per violation; Attorney General and district attorneys enforcement authority
exceptions: Small businesses processing data of fewer than 100,000 consumers annually
Employment and B2B data have limited exemptions in some contexts
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Attorney General Privacy Act Resources

quiz.q: What unique feature does Colorado's Privacy Act include compared to many state privacy laws?
options: It requires privacy agents in every company
quiz.explanation: Unlike many other state privacy laws, Colorado's Privacy Act applies to nonprofit organizations, extending privacy obligations beyond for-profit commercial entities.

laws.title: SB 205 AI in Consequential Decisions Act
laws.subtitle: Colorado became the first US state to regulate AI in high-stakes decisions
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's SB 205 (2024), the Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act, became the first US state law regulating AI use in 'consequential decisions' — defined as decisions significantly affecting employment, education, housing, credit, healthcare, and insurance. Developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems must implement risk management practices, conduct algorithmic impact assessments, and provide consumer disclosures. Consumers have rights to appeal AI-based decisions and request human review. The Governor signed it with reservations, calling on the legislature to refine it before it takes effect in 2026. The law drew intense debate about balancing innovation with consumer protection.
laws.penalty: Violations of consumer disclosure and risk assessment requirements: civil enforcement by the Attorney General; fines up to $20,000 per violation
exceptions: Small businesses with AI systems below specified impact thresholds
AI tools used solely for internal administrative functions

quiz.q: What year does Colorado's AI Act (SB 205) take effect?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's SB 205 Artificial Intelligence Act was signed in 2024 but takes effect in 2026, giving the legislature and industry time to potentially refine the law before enforcement begins.

laws.title: Colorado AI Act — High-Risk AI Systems
laws.subtitle: Colorado enacts first comprehensive state AI law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's SB 205 (2024) is the first comprehensive state law regulating high-risk AI systems — those that make or assist consequential decisions in employment, housing, credit, education, healthcare, and insurance. Developers must use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination. Deployers must conduct impact assessments, maintain risk management policies, and disclose AI use. Consumers have rights to appeal adverse AI decisions.
laws.penalty: Enforced by Colorado Attorney General; civil penalties; private right of action in some cases
exceptions: AI in national security
Research and development
Small businesses below thresholds

quiz.q: What is Colorado SB 205 significant for?
options: Being the first comprehensive state AI law covering high-risk systems
quiz.explanation: Colorado SB 205 was the first comprehensive U.S. state law to regulate high-risk AI systems across multiple sectors including employment, housing, and healthcare.

laws.title: Colorado Methane Reduction Rules
laws.subtitle: Colorado leads nation in oil and gas methane regulations
laws.fullDescription: Colorado was among the first states to enact comprehensive rules targeting methane emissions from oil and gas operations. The Colorado Air Quality Control Commission adopted Regulation 7 requirements that mandate leak detection and repair (LDAR) programs, emission control equipment on new and existing facilities, and quarterly inspections. Colorado also enacted Senate Bill 181 (2019) giving local governments more authority over oil and gas siting, and created the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission.
laws.penalty: Violations of methane rules: fines up to $15,000 per day; permit revocation for serious non-compliance
exceptions: Stripper wells below daily production thresholds
Research facilities
Inactive wells undergoing proper plugging

quiz.q: What did Colorado Senate Bill 181 (2019) give local governments regarding oil and gas?
options: Power to levy taxes on oil production
More authority over oil and gas siting decisions
The ability to ban fracking statewide
quiz.explanation: Colorado SB 181 gave local governments significantly more authority to regulate oil and gas siting, including the ability to establish setback distances and additional local protections.

laws.title: Colorado Red Flag Law
laws.subtitle: Colorado allows courts to temporarily remove guns from dangerous individuals
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Extreme Risk Protection Order (ERPO) law, known as a red flag law, allows family members, law enforcement, and household members to petition a court to temporarily remove firearms from an individual who poses a significant risk to themselves or others. A court must approve the petition, and the subject has the right to a hearing. Colorado's law has been used in cases involving domestic violence threats, potential mass shootings, and suicide risk. Some county sheriffs declared they would not enforce the law.
laws.penalty: Violating an ERPO by not surrendering firearms: class 1 misdemeanor; making false statements in ERPO petition: criminal penalties
exceptions: The subject can petition for return of firearms after the risk period
Temporary orders require full hearing within 14 days
Due process protections apply throughout

quiz.q: Who can petition for an Extreme Risk Protection Order in Colorado?
options: Family members, law enforcement, and household members
quiz.explanation: Colorado's red flag law allows family members, law enforcement officers, and household members to petition a court for an Extreme Risk Protection Order to temporarily remove firearms from a person posing significant risk.

laws.title: Colorado Privacy Act
laws.subtitle: Colorado enacts broad consumer privacy protection
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Privacy Act (CPA, effective July 2023) gives Colorado consumers rights to access, correct, delete, and opt out of the sale or targeted advertising of their personal data. Businesses that process data of 100,000+ Colorado consumers or process 25,000+ consumers' data for profit must comply. The Attorney General enforces the law, with a 60-day cure period before enforcement action. Colorado also requires privacy risk assessments for certain processing activities.
laws.penalty: Attorney General enforcement: injunctive relief and civil penalties; no private right of action initially; willful violations face enhanced penalties
exceptions: Employee data
Publicly available information
Non-commercial processing for research and journalism

quiz.q: What minimum threshold triggers Colorado Privacy Act obligations for data processors?
options: Any processing of Colorado resident data
Processing data of 100,000 or more Colorado consumers
Having a physical location in Colorado
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Privacy Act applies to businesses that control or process personal data of 100,000 or more Colorado consumers, or businesses that process 25,000 or more consumers' data and derive revenue from selling personal data.

laws.title: Colorado AI Act
laws.subtitle: Colorado's law imposing duties on high-risk AI developers and deployers
laws.fullDescription: Colorado became the first US state to enact comprehensive artificial intelligence regulation with the Colorado AI Act (SB 205), focused on high-risk AI systems that make consequential decisions in areas like employment, housing, credit, education, insurance, and healthcare. Developers must use reasonable care to protect against algorithmic discrimination. Deployers must conduct impact assessments, disclose when AI is used in consequential decisions, provide meaningful explanation for adverse decisions, and create a process for consumers to appeal AI-driven decisions. The law takes effect in 2026.
laws.penalty: Violations can be enforced by the Attorney General as unfair trade practices carrying civil penalties of up to $20,000 per violation; consumers can file individual complaints
exceptions: Non-high-risk AI uses have no obligations under the law
Covered entities with fewer than 50 employees have simplified requirements
National security and law enforcement AI follow federal frameworks

quiz.q: What was significant about Colorado's AI Act (SB 205) nationally?
options: It banned AI use in government entirely
It was the first comprehensive US state AI regulation focused on high-risk AI systems
It required all AI to be open-source
It mandated AI be made in the USA
quiz.explanation: Colorado's AI Act was the first comprehensive state AI law in the United States, focused specifically on high-risk AI systems making consequential decisions, and has been studied as a model by other states considering similar legislation.

laws.title: Colorado Proposition 123 Affordable Housing
laws.subtitle: Colorado's dedicated affordable housing funding from income tax
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters approved Proposition 123, dedicating a portion of existing state income tax revenue (0.1% of taxable income) to affordable housing programs. The measure does not raise taxes but redirects existing revenue to fund grants and loans for affordable housing development, down payment assistance, and local government housing programs. Participating local governments must commit to accelerating affordable housing approvals. The measure was expected to generate approximately $300 million annually for affordable housing. Colorado has faced severe housing affordability crises particularly along the Front Range.
laws.penalty: Local governments that commit to accelerated approvals under Prop 123 and then fail to deliver face consequences in future funding eligibility; misuse of Prop 123 funds triggers state audit and repayment requirements
exceptions: Luxury housing developments are not eligible for Prop 123 subsidies
Vacation and short-term rental units cannot use Prop 123 funding
Local governments that choose not to participate can opt out of the accelerated approval requirement

quiz.q: How does Colorado's Proposition 123 fund affordable housing without raising taxes?
options: By issuing state bonds backed by housing appreciation
By taxing real estate transactions above certain values
By redirecting 0.1% of existing income tax revenue
By charging impact fees on luxury development
quiz.explanation: Prop 123 funds affordable housing by redirecting 0.1% of existing state income tax revenue that would otherwise go to the general fund — not a new tax, but a dedicated allocation of existing revenue, which voters approved directly through the ballot initiative.

laws.title: National Popular Vote Interstate Compact
laws.subtitle: Colorado's participation in an effort to elect presidents by popular vote
laws.fullDescription: Colorado joined the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, agreeing to award its electoral votes to the presidential candidate who wins the national popular vote rather than just Colorado's popular vote — but only once states representing 270 or more electoral votes have joined the compact. The compact is designed to effectively implement popular vote presidential elections without a constitutional amendment. Colorado voters approved the measure in a 2020 referendum. Participating states have a combined electoral vote count of over 200, still short of the 270 needed for activation.
laws.penalty: State election officials who fail to award electoral votes according to compact requirements would be in violation of state law; compact withdrawal within a specified pre-election window is restricted
exceptions: The compact only activates when states totaling 270 electoral votes have joined
Colorado can withdraw from the compact outside the restricted pre-election window
Presidential primaries in Colorado are not affected by the NPV compact

quiz.q: Under what condition does the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact actually take effect?
options: Immediately upon enough states joining to form a majority
Once states representing 270 or more electoral votes have joined
After three consecutive elections using the current electoral college system
When the Supreme Court rules the current system unconstitutional
quiz.explanation: The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact only activates when member states collectively represent 270 or more electoral votes — the threshold for winning the presidency — ensuring the compact doesn't take effect unless it would actually determine the election outcome.

laws.title: Colorado AI Act - High-Risk Artificial Intelligence Systems
laws.subtitle: First comprehensive US state AI regulation for consequential decisions
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted SB 205 (2024), the first comprehensive US state law regulating high-risk AI systems used to make consequential decisions affecting housing, employment, financial services, education, and healthcare. The law requires developers to disclose known risks, perform bias impact assessments, and notify consumers when AI is used in decisions affecting them. Deployers must maintain risk management policies and allow consumers to appeal automated decisions. The law was modeled on the EU AI Act.
laws.penalty: Violations of Colorado's AI Act constitute deceptive trade practices under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act: fines up to $20,000 per violation. Willful violations: up to $100,000 per violation.
exceptions: AI systems used for research or development not deployed in consequential decisions exempt
AI used in cybersecurity operations and anti-fraud systems have modified disclosure requirements
Small businesses under 25 employees have extended compliance timelines

quiz.q: What was Colorado's SB 205 modeled on internationally?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's AI Act (SB 205, 2024) was modeled on the EU AI Act, making it the first comprehensive US state law regulating high-risk AI systems used for consequential decisions in housing, employment, financial services, education, and healthcare.

laws.title: Colorado FAMLI Paid Family and Medical Leave Program
laws.subtitle: State-run paid leave insurance program launching 2024
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) program began paying benefits in January 2024 after collection of premiums since January 2023. The program provides up to 12 weeks of paid leave for workers to care for a new child, serious illness, or family emergency, replacing up to 90% of wages for low-wage workers (up to $1,100 per week cap). Both employers and employees split the 0.9% premium. Colorado became one of a growing number of states creating state-run paid leave programs as federal action has stalled.
laws.penalty: Employers who fail to remit FAMLI premiums: fines of $50 per employee per day of non-compliance. Employers who retaliate against workers for using FAMLI leave: civil liability including reinstatement and 3x damages.
exceptions: Employers with under 10 employees pay only the employee portion of premiums (not the employer portion)
Self-employed workers may opt in voluntarily to the program
Federal government employees covered by separate federal FMLA provisions

quiz.q: What percentage of wages does Colorado's FAMLI program replace for the lowest-wage workers?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's FAMLI program replaces up to 90% of wages for low-wage workers (those earning below 50% of the state average weekly wage), tapering to lower percentages for higher earners. This high replacement rate was designed to make paid leave financially feasible for workers who previously couldn't afford to take unpaid time off.

laws.title: Colorado Housing Affordability and Land Use Reform
laws.subtitle: State preemption of local zoning near transit
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted HB 23-1190 (Transit-Oriented Communities) in 2024, requiring cities and counties near transit stations to allow multifamily housing in their zoning codes or face state preemption. Cities near rail transit stations must allow buildings of at least 3 stories within a quarter-mile, while bus rapid transit corridors have lower requirements. Colorado joined a growing number of states using state authority to override local zoning exclusion to address housing affordability.
laws.penalty: Local governments that fail to adopt compliant zoning ordinances by the deadline: state authority to approve qualifying housing developments directly through the Department of Local Affairs.
exceptions: Communities with population under 1,000 subject to simplified compliance standards
Historic designation areas within transit corridors subject to compatibility review process
Industrial zones posing health risks exempt from residential requirement until remediated

quiz.q: What must cities near rail transit stations allow within a quarter-mile under Colorado's transit-oriented communities law?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's transit-oriented communities law (HB 23-1190) requires cities near rail transit stations to allow multifamily buildings of at least 3 stories within a quarter-mile of the station — using state authority to override local zoning exclusions that had prevented dense housing development near transit.

laws.title: Colorado Privacy Act (CPA) – Comprehensive Consumer Privacy
laws.subtitle: Colorado enacts comprehensive data privacy rights law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Privacy Act gave residents rights to access, correct, delete, and opt out of the sale of their personal data. It applied to businesses processing data of 100,000+ consumers per year. Colorado's law went further than Virginia's by requiring opt-in consent for sensitive data processing and including a universal opt-out mechanism provision. The law took effect in July 2023.
laws.penalty: Violations: civil penalties up to $20,000 per violation enforced by Attorney General; no private right of action
exceptions: HIPAA-covered entities and data fully governed by HIPAA exempt
Non-profit organisations exempt from the law's requirements

quiz.q: How many consumers' data must a business process annually before Colorado's Privacy Act applies to them?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Privacy Act applies to businesses that control or process personal data of 100,000 or more Colorado consumers per year, or derive revenue from selling data of 25,000+ consumers.

laws.title: Colorado AI Act – Risk-Based AI Regulation
laws.subtitle: Colorado becomes first US state with comprehensive AI risk law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted the first US state law creating a risk-based regulatory framework for AI systems, requiring developers and deployers of 'high-risk AI systems' to conduct impact assessments, manage bias risks, notify consumers when AI is used for consequential decisions, and provide appeal mechanisms. The law applied to AI used in employment, credit, insurance, housing, and healthcare.
laws.penalty: Violations: civil penalties enforced by Attorney General up to $20,000 per violation
exceptions: AI used for national security purposes exempt
Open-source AI models with no commercial deployment not covered

quiz.q: In what domains does Colorado's AI Act apply to 'high-risk' AI systems?
options: Employment, credit, insurance, housing, and healthcare
quiz.explanation: Colorado's AI Act applies to high-risk AI systems used in consequential domains including employment, credit, insurance, housing, and healthcare — areas where AI decisions significantly impact people's lives.

laws.title: Colorado River Compact Renegotiation
laws.subtitle: Colorado joins seven-state deal to reduce river diversions
laws.fullDescription: Colorado joined the other six Colorado River Basin states and the federal government in a new water sharing agreement as the Colorado River faced historically low levels. Colorado agreed to mandatory reductions in water diversions, funded agricultural water leasing programmes to pay farmers to temporarily falllow fields, and enacted water conservation requirements for municipalities. The agreement replaced emergency deadlock measures.
laws.penalty: Water districts exceeding their mandatory reduction targets: loss of federal water infrastructure funding; illegal diversions: criminal prosecution
exceptions: Tribal water rights protected under separate federal trust doctrine
Existing hydropower operations receive transitional accommodations

quiz.q: How many states share the Colorado River Basin under the renegotiated compact?
quiz.explanation: Seven states share the Colorado River Basin — Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico (upper basin) and California, Nevada, Arizona (lower basin) — along with Mexico, and all participated in renegotiating water sharing as the river reached historically low levels.

laws.title: Colorado River Compact Reform and Water Scarcity Emergency Act
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for Colorado River rationing
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted the Colorado River Water Security and Scarcity Emergency Act 2025 following the Colorado River Compact renegotiation crisis as Lake Mead and Lake Powell dropped to historically low levels. The law establishes Colorado's water rights priority system under compact reform negotiations, creates a Water Bank allowing temporary water rights transfers between agricultural and municipal users, mandates 15% agricultural water use efficiency improvements by 2027 through subsidized irrigation technology, authorizes direct potable reuse (drinking reclaimed water) for the first time in Colorado's history, and establishes a Drought Emergency Reserve Fund. Colorado's upstream position in the basin creates complex interstate obligations.
laws.penalty: Water rights violation during declared scarcity emergency: forfeiture of rights plus $50,000/acre-foot taken; illegal groundwater pumping above permit: $100,000 per day; false water use reporting: 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Senior water rights holders receive priority under prior appropriation doctrine
Tribal water rights protected under federal trust responsibility
Emergency firefighting water use exempt from scarcity restrictions

quiz.q: What historic first does Colorado's Water Security Act authorize for the first time in the state's history?
options: Direct potable reuse of reclaimed water
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Water Security and Scarcity Emergency Act authorizes direct potable reuse — treating and drinking reclaimed wastewater — for the first time in Colorado's history, as an essential tool for water supply in the arid, drought-stressed West.

laws.title: Colorado AI Consumer Protection and Algorithmic Transparency Act
laws.subtitle: Balancing AI innovation with consumer rights
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted the AI Consumer Protection and Algorithmic Transparency Act 2025, building on its 2024 SB 205 AI framework. The law extends algorithmic transparency requirements to AI systems used in insurance pricing, real estate assessments, and consumer lending, creates a Consumer AI Rights Declaration establishing rights to explanation, correction, and human review of AI decisions, establishes the Colorado AI Innovation Office promoting responsible AI development in state's tech sector, introduces a voluntary AI Safety Certification that reduces regulatory scrutiny for compliant companies, and mandates AI impact statements for all state government AI procurement above $500,000.
laws.penalty: Insurance AI pricing non-disclosure: $500,000 per consumer affected; consumer right to explanation denial: $10,000 per violation; false AI Safety Certification: $2 million plus criminal referral
exceptions: AI systems used for cybersecurity monitoring exempt from transparency requirements
Academic AI research tools have modified consumer disclosure framework
Emergency AI use in natural disaster response has simplified compliance pathway

quiz.q: Colorado's 2025 AI Consumer Protection Act extends transparency requirements specifically to which insurance sector application?
options: AI systems used in insurance pricing
quiz.explanation: Colorado's AI Consumer Protection Act specifically targets AI systems used in insurance pricing — extending transparency requirements to ensure consumers know when algorithmic systems are determining their insurance rates and can challenge discriminatory pricing.

laws.title: Colorado Affordable Housing and Ski Town Crisis Act
laws.subtitle: Addressing workforce housing collapse in mountain communities
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted the Affordable Housing Emergency and Mountain Community Workforce Act 2025, responding to the acute housing crisis in ski resort towns where essential workers cannot afford to live. The law creates the Colorado Mountain Community Housing Authority with power to acquire land for deed-restricted workforce housing, mandates that ski resorts above 500,000 annual skier visits contribute 5% of lift ticket revenues to a regional workforce housing fund, establishes Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) by-right approval throughout mountain counties removing local veto, creates the Short-Term Rental Impact Fee on Airbnb and VRBO rentals in mountain counties directing 50% of fees to workforce housing, and introduces employer-sponsored housing tax credits for mountain businesses.
laws.penalty: Ski resort housing fund non-compliance: loss of ski resort operating permits in Colorado; STR impact fee evasion: 300% unpaid fee plus $50,000; ADU permit denial by county: state override plus $100,000
exceptions: Small ski areas under 100,000 annual visitors have reduced housing fund contribution
Owner-occupied STRs renting fewer than 90 days/year have reduced impact fee
Historic structures and sensitive preservation sites have modified ADU requirements

quiz.q: What percentage of lift ticket revenues must large Colorado ski resorts contribute to regional workforce housing funds under the 2025 Act?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Affordable Housing and Mountain Community Act requires ski resorts with over 500,000 annual skier visits to contribute 5% of lift ticket revenues to regional workforce housing funds — a direct link between the ski industry's profitability and solutions for the housing crisis it partly creates.

laws.title: Colorado River Water Conservation and Drought Emergency Act
laws.subtitle: Mandatory water use reductions amid historic drought
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted mandatory water conservation legislation in response to Lake Powell and Lake Mead reaching historically low levels. The law requires municipalities to reduce water consumption by 15% from 2020 baseline levels, restricts new water-intensive development in the Colorado River watershed, creates incentives for agricultural water sharing programs with cities, and establishes a state water resilience fund for infrastructure upgrades.
laws.penalty: Municipalities that exceed water allocation limits face fines of $500 per acre-foot of excess use. Developers who build water-intensive projects without approved supply plans face project injunctions.
exceptions: Agricultural operations with senior water rights established before 1922 retain their allocations under prior appropriation doctrine
Tribal nations with reserved water rights are not subject to the mandatory reduction requirements

quiz.q: What two major reservoirs on the Colorado River have reached historically low levels prompting water conservation legislation?
quiz.explanation: Lake Powell (behind Glen Canyon Dam) and Lake Mead (behind Hoover Dam) are the two largest reservoirs on the Colorado River. Both reached critically low levels due to prolonged drought and overallocation, threatening water supplies for 40 million people.

laws.title: Psychedelic Therapy and Natural Medicine Regulation Act
laws.subtitle: Implementing voter-approved psilocybin services
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted implementing legislation for Proposition 122 passed by voters, which created a regulated system for therapeutic use of psilocybin and other natural medicines at licensed healing centers. The law establishes licensing for facilitators and healing centers, creates training requirements, sets safety protocols, establishes age requirements (21+), and creates a regulatory body. Colorado became the second US state after Oregon to create a regulated therapeutic psilocybin system.
laws.penalty: Operating a psilocybin healing center without a license carries up to 18 months imprisonment. Providing psilocybin to minors carries up to five years. Distribution outside the licensed framework carries standard drug distribution penalties.
exceptions: Indigenous ceremonial use of natural plant medicines in traditional religious contexts retains legal protection
Personal cultivation of psilocybin mushrooms for personal use by adults is decriminalized in Colorado

quiz.q: What did Colorado voters approve in Proposition 122 that the new law implements?
options: Full recreational psilocybin sales in dispensaries
A regulated system for therapeutic psilocybin use at healing centers
quiz.explanation: Colorado voters approved Proposition 122 in 2022, creating a regulated system where licensed healing centers can provide supervised therapeutic psilocybin sessions to adults — not recreational sales, but therapeutic use with a trained facilitator.

laws.title: Sports Betting Revenue and Problem Gambling Prevention Act
laws.subtitle: Regulating Colorado's legalized sports betting market
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted comprehensive sports betting regulation following voter approval of Proposition DD. The law establishes the licensing framework for online and retail sportsbooks, dedicates a portion of tax revenue to water conservation (as specified by voters), creates a robust problem gambling treatment program, requires geolocation verification, mandates responsible gambling tools in all apps, and establishes advertising restrictions.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed sports betting operations face fines up to $100,000 per day. Licensed operators who accept bets from minors face license revocation. Match-fixing by athletes faces up to five years imprisonment.
exceptions: Fantasy sports with entry fees under $10 retain their separate classification outside sports betting regulation
Tribal casinos that signed compacts before Proposition DD retain their independently negotiated sports betting frameworks

quiz.q: What environmental purpose did Colorado voters direct sports betting tax revenues toward?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Proposition DD, which legalized sports betting, specified that a portion of tax revenues would go to water conservation projects — reflecting Colorado's increasing concerns about drought and water scarcity in the Colorado River basin.

laws.title: Colorado AI Systems in High-Risk Decision Making Act
laws.subtitle: Algorithmic Accountability and Bias Auditing Law
laws.fullDescription: Requires developers and deployers of AI systems used in consequential decisions to conduct impact assessments and disclose AI use to affected individuals. The law covers employment, housing, credit, healthcare, and insurance decisions, mandates annual bias audits, requires human review availability, creates anti-discrimination protections, and establishes enforcement through the state attorney general.
laws.penalty: Civil penalties up to $20,000 per violation; injunctive relief; attorney general enforcement
exceptions: AI systems used solely for internal administrative purposes
Research and development AI not deployed for consequential decisions

quiz.q: What must Colorado AI systems used for consequential decisions have annually?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's AI Act mandates annual bias audits for AI systems used in consequential decisions like employment, housing, and credit.

laws.title: Colorado Proposition 128 and Violent Offender Parole Reform Act
laws.subtitle: Earned Time and Victims Rights Balancing Law
laws.fullDescription: Implements voter-approved Proposition 128 restricting earned time credits for violent offenders while maintaining rehabilitation programs. The law limits sentence reductions for murder, sexual assault, and child abuse convictions, establishes victim notification requirements before any early release, creates earned time for programming and education, and balances public safety concerns with rehabilitation goals.
laws.penalty: Administrative sanctions for DOC officials granting unauthorized earned time; appeals process for denied credits
exceptions: Terminal illness and compassionate release follow separate humanitarian process
Juvenile offenders sentenced as adults have modified provisions

quiz.q: What does Colorado's Proposition 128 restrict for violent offenders?
options: Earned time credits for sentence reduction
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Proposition 128 restricts earned time credits that reduce sentences for violent offenders like murderers and sexual assault perpetrators.

laws.title: Colorado Healthy Homes and Indoor Air Quality Standards Act
laws.subtitle: Indoor Environmental Quality and Wildfire Smoke Law
laws.fullDescription: Establishes indoor air quality standards for Colorado residences and buildings following increased wildfire smoke events. The law mandates smoke-resistant ventilation in new construction, creates rebate programs for air purifiers in low-income communities, establishes school air quality monitoring, creates disclosure requirements for renters about building air filtration capabilities, and funds weatherization improvements for energy efficiency and air quality.
laws.penalty: Fines for new construction failing ventilation standards; disclosure penalties for landlords
exceptions: Historic buildings have alternative compliance pathways
Rural buildings in low-smoke areas have simplified requirements

quiz.q: What specific environmental event has driven Colorado's indoor air quality standards?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Indoor Air Quality Act was driven by increasing wildfire smoke events that have degraded air quality throughout the Rocky Mountain region.

laws.title: Colorado Fentanyl Accountability and Prevention Act
laws.subtitle: Overdose Crisis and Drug Trafficking Law
laws.fullDescription: Strengthens Colorado's response to the fentanyl overdose epidemic with enhanced criminal penalties and treatment investments. The law creates enhanced penalties for fentanyl distribution causing death, establishes fentanyl test strip legalization and distribution programs, creates naloxone distribution requirements for pharmacies and schools, establishes drug checking services, and funds community-based overdose prevention programs.
laws.penalty: Up to 32 years for fentanyl distribution causing death; enhanced penalties for sales near schools
exceptions: Personal use amounts have diversion to treatment rather than incarceration
Overdose reporters receive Good Samaritan protection

quiz.q: What protection does Colorado's Fentanyl Act extend to people who call for overdose help?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Fentanyl Accountability Act extends Good Samaritan protection to people who call for help during overdoses, encouraging life-saving calls.

laws.title: Psilocybin Therapy Licensing Program
laws.subtitle: Colorado Becomes Second State to Allow Psychedelic Therapy
laws.fullDescription: Colorado launched its regulated psilocybin therapy licensing program following voter approval of Proposition 122 in 2022, allowing licensed healing centers to administer psilocybin mushrooms under trained facilitator supervision.
laws.penalty: Criminal penalties for unlicensed psilocybin services
exceptions: Licensed healing centers
Personal cultivation decriminalized for adults

quiz.q: What did Colorado legalize with Proposition 122?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Proposition 122 legalized psilocybin mushroom therapy at licensed healing centers.

laws.title: Extreme Risk Protection Order Expansion
laws.subtitle: Colorado Strengthens Red Flag Gun Law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado expanded its extreme risk protection order (red flag) law to allow more individuals including coworkers, employers, and healthcare providers to petition courts to temporarily remove firearms from people deemed a danger to themselves or others. The law had been credited with preventing suicides and mass shootings.
laws.penalty: Court-ordered temporary firearm removal; criminal penalties for ERPO violations
exceptions: Due process hearing requirements
Firearm return when threat resolved

quiz.q: What are extreme risk protection orders designed to do?
options: Temporarily remove firearms from people deemed a danger
quiz.explanation: Extreme risk protection orders temporarily remove firearms from individuals a court determines pose a danger to themselves or others, with due process protections.

laws.title: Colorado River Water Rights Compact Update
laws.subtitle: Colorado Negotiates Upper Basin Water Management
laws.fullDescription: Colorado led negotiations among upper Colorado River basin states (Colorado, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico) for updated water use rules as Lake Powell and Lake Mead declined. The states agreed to demand management programs reducing consumption in exchange for federal funding. Colorado's agricultural water users bore significant sacrifice.
laws.penalty: Federal Bureau of Reclamation delivery reductions; compact compliance requirements
exceptions: Municipal priority water rights
Tribal water rights settlements

quiz.q: What are the upper Colorado River Basin states?
quiz.explanation: The upper Colorado River Basin states are Colorado, Wyoming, Utah, and New Mexico, which negotiated demand management programs to reduce consumption.

laws.title: Insulin Price Cap and Drug Affordability
laws.subtitle: Colorado Limits Insulin Copays to $100 Per Month
