laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted one of the nation's strongest insulin price cap laws, limiting out-of-pocket insulin costs to $100 per 30-day supply for insured patients. The law preceded federal action. Colorado also created a state drug importation program from Canada for other high-cost medications.
laws.penalty: Insurance plan violations subject to state enforcement
exceptions: Uninsured patients have separate assistance programs
Federal programs in addition to state

quiz.q: What does Colorado's insulin price cap limit monthly costs to?
quiz.explanation: Colorado capped insulin out-of-pocket costs at $100 per 30-day supply for insured patients, one of the nation's strongest insulin affordability laws.

laws.title: Space Industry and Aerospace Cluster
laws.subtitle: Colorado Builds National Aerospace Hub
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Front Range became one of the nation's top aerospace and space industry clusters, with Lockheed Martin, Ball Aerospace, United Launch Alliance, and numerous startups. The US Space Command, several military space units, and commercial space companies made Colorado a space industry center.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; export control compliance for space tech
exceptions: Defense space contracts subject to security clearances
ITAR export restrictions

quiz.q: What military organization made Colorado a key hub for national space activities?
quiz.explanation: US Space Command, headquartered in Colorado, along with numerous military space units and commercial companies, established Colorado as a major space industry hub.

laws.title: Colorado River Crisis and Water Compact Renegotiation
laws.subtitle: Seven states fight over a river that no longer reaches the sea
laws.fullDescription: The Colorado River, which supplies water to 40 million people in seven US states and Mexico, is in severe crisis. The river no longer reaches the sea. Lake Mead and Lake Powell, the two largest US reservoirs, hit historically low levels from drought and overuse. States are renegotiating the 1922 Colorado River Compact that allocated more water than actually flows. Agriculture (80% of use) faces cuts. Cities like Las Vegas and Phoenix implement conservation. Climate change is permanently reducing snowpack.
laws.penalty: States that use more than their compact allocation face mandatory cuts under shortage declarations
exceptions: Tribal water rights were not fully included in the 1922 compact and are being renegotiated separately
Mexico receives guaranteed minimum flow under 1944 treaty regardless of shortage

laws.title: Wildfire Mitigation and Forest Health Crisis
laws.subtitle: Colorado battles unprecedented wildfire risk from beetle kill and drought
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's forests face a triple threat: bark beetle kill has damaged millions of acres of pine forests creating massive standing dead fuel loads, drought has stressed remaining trees, and climate-driven heat creates longer, hotter fire seasons. The Marshall Fire (2021) destroyed over 1,000 homes in suburban Boulder County — a suburban fire, not backcountry. Colorado's wildfire mitigation program requires forest thinning, defensible space creation, and building code upgrades. Insurance companies are reassessing coverage in high-risk zones.
laws.penalty: Homeowners in wildland-urban interface zones must create defensible space or face fines
exceptions: Properties predating wildfire code adoption may have grandfather provisions
Agricultural burning permits continue with notification requirements

laws.title: Outdoor Recreation Economy and Public Lands Economy
laws.subtitle: Colorado leads US in outdoor recreation as economic driver
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generates $38+ billion annually — skiing, hiking, climbing, cycling, fishing, and camping. The state created the first Office of Outdoor Recreation Industry in the US to support the sector. Colorado's public lands (national forests, parks, BLM lands) are economic assets attracting residents and businesses. Remote work from mountain towns (Breckenridge, Telluride, Steamboat Springs) is reshaping demographics. Colorado's outdoor brand attracts tech companies seeking to recruit talent that values lifestyle.
laws.penalty: Trail use and park access may require reservation systems during peak periods to manage overcrowding
exceptions: Search and rescue volunteers have unrestricted access to wilderness areas
Wilderness stewardship volunteers exempt from standard group size limits

quiz.q: How much does Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generate annually?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generates over $38 billion annually — making skiing, hiking, cycling, and other outdoor activities a core economic engine comparable to traditional industries.

laws.title: Water Rights Crisis and Colorado River Compact Renegotiation
laws.subtitle: Colorado and Western states facing existential water shortage
laws.fullDescription: Colorado sits at the headwaters of the Colorado River, which supplies water to seven US states and Mexico under the 1922 Colorado River Compact — negotiated when flow estimates were too optimistic. Decades of overallocation, climate change-driven drought, and population growth have created a crisis where more water is legally allocated than the river can provide in most years. Lake Mead and Lake Powell, the river's two major reservoirs, hit dangerously low levels in recent years. The federal government mandated water cuts for Arizona, Nevada, and eventually California. Colorado's own water rights system — based on prior appropriation (first in time, first in right) — creates complex negotiations between agricultural users (who hold most senior rights) and growing urban areas. Denver and other Front Range cities must import water over the Continental Divide. Colorado has invested in water efficiency and storage while negotiating the future Colorado River framework.
laws.penalty: Unauthorized water use carries fines and required repayment; senior water rights can enforce against junior users through state water courts
exceptions: Domestic and municipal uses have some priority protections over agricultural in emergency shortage scenarios

quiz.q: What fundamental problem exists with the 1922 Colorado River Compact?
options: It was never ratified by all seven states
It allocated water based on flow estimates that proved too optimistic
It excluded Mexico from any water share
It gave too much authority to the federal government
quiz.explanation: The 1922 Colorado River Compact was negotiated using flow estimates that proved too optimistic — more water was legally allocated among seven states than the river actually produces in most years, creating chronic overallocation.

laws.title: Aerospace and Space Industry Hub
laws.subtitle: Colorado hosting space command, major contractors, and commercial space
laws.fullDescription: Colorado hosts an extraordinary concentration of space industry assets: US Space Command and Space Force headquarters are in Colorado Springs, NORAD is at Cheyenne Mountain, Lockheed Martin's Space division is in Littleton, United Launch Alliance is in Centennial, and dozens of smaller space companies cluster throughout the Front Range. The commercial space boom has expanded this ecosystem dramatically, with companies like Sierra Space and others developing next-generation spacecraft and habitats. Colorado receives more federal space spending per capita than virtually any other state. The University of Colorado Boulder has a significant space research program including the Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics. Denver International Airport's central location and a highly educated workforce make Colorado attractive for aerospace executives. The space industry intertwines with Colorado's significant defense sector.
laws.penalty: Space activities require FAA licensing for commercial launches; defense-related activities operate under classified security frameworks
exceptions: Academic and research satellite activities have simplified licensing procedures

quiz.q: Which major US military command related to space is headquartered in Colorado Springs?
quiz.explanation: US Space Command, which oversees military space operations, is headquartered in Colorado Springs, alongside US Space Force components and NORAD at nearby Cheyenne Mountain — making Colorado the center of US military space operations.

laws.title: Ski Industry Contraction and Mountain Community Adaptation
laws.subtitle: Colorado ski towns diversifying as climate threatens snowpack
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's ski industry generates approximately $5 billion annually and supports communities throughout the Rocky Mountains, but climate change is reducing snowpack and shortening the ski season. Average Colorado snowpack has declined over decades, with more precipitation falling as rain rather than snow at lower elevations. Ski resorts have responded with massive snowmaking investments, summer activity development, and marketing of year-round mountain experiences. Vail Resorts and other operators have pursued international expansion to diversify away from Colorado's climate risk. Some smaller ski areas have been forced to close. The transformation of mountain communities — from pure ski towns to four-season destinations — requires significant investment in hiking, biking, festivals, and arts infrastructure. Affordable housing in ski towns is an acute crisis, as workers cannot afford to live in the communities they serve.
laws.penalty: Ski area operations require Forest Service permits on federal land; water rights for snowmaking must be obtained
exceptions: Some Native American tribal rights to traditional mountain areas intersect with ski resort operations

quiz.q: Approximately how much does Colorado's ski industry generate annually?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's ski industry generates approximately $5 billion annually and supports mountain communities throughout the Rockies, but climate change is reducing snowpack and forcing the industry to diversify into four-season recreation.

laws.title: TABOR and Fiscal Constraints
laws.subtitle: Taxpayer Bill of Rights limits government spending growth
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Taxpayer Bill of Rights (TABOR), passed by referendum in 1992, requires voter approval for tax increases and limits government revenue growth to inflation plus population growth. Excess revenue is refunded to taxpayers. TABOR has constrained Colorado's ability to fund transportation, education and other needs despite the state's explosive population growth. Supporters see it as taxpayer protection; critics argue it has crippled public investment. Colorado regularly navigates budget constraints through creative accounting and selective voter override requests.
laws.penalty: Government agencies cannot retain excess revenue beyond TABOR limits without voter approval
exceptions: Voters can approve specific enterprise funds and revenue retentions
Federal grants and matching funds not subject to TABOR limitations

quiz.q: What does Colorado's TABOR require before the government can raise taxes?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Taxpayer Bill of Rights (TABOR) requires voter approval through referendum before the government can raise taxes, making it one of the most restrictive fiscal constraints any US state government faces.

laws.title: Colorado AI Act
laws.subtitle: First comprehensive state AI regulation becomes law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado enacted the Colorado AI Act in 2024, becoming the first US state to pass comprehensive AI regulation covering high-risk AI systems. The law requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination, conduct impact assessments and provide appeal mechanisms for consequential AI decisions. Governor Jared Polis signed the bill despite significant technology industry opposition, though with a delayed implementation date giving businesses time to prepare.
laws.penalty: Violations of AI Act requirements subject to investigation and enforcement by Colorado Attorney General
exceptions: AI systems posing low risk exempt from most requirements
Small businesses have modified compliance obligations

quiz.q: What made the Colorado AI Act historically significant in the US regulatory landscape?
options: It was the first federal AI regulation
It was the first state to ban AI hiring tools
It was the first comprehensive state AI regulation covering high-risk systems
It imposed the world's largest AI fines
quiz.explanation: The Colorado AI Act was the first comprehensive state AI regulation in the US, covering high-risk AI systems used in consequential decisions about employment, housing, credit and healthcare—though it faced significant technology industry opposition.

laws.title: Outdoor Recreation Economy
laws.subtitle: Colorado's mountains drive billion-dollar tourism and outdoor industry
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generates over $60 billion annually, making it among the nation's largest. Skiing, hiking, mountain biking, camping and rafting draw visitors from across the country. The ski industry employs tens of thousands and supports resort towns. However climate change is threatening the ski season with reduced and later snowpack. Some resorts have invested heavily in snowmaking while others in lower elevations face existential threats. The outdoor recreation sector increasingly drives Colorado's politics around public lands and climate policy.
laws.penalty: Wilderness areas and national parks have use restrictions; backcountry permits required for popular routes to manage overcrowding
exceptions: Local residents have different access provisions for some public lands
Commercial operators require separate outfitter licenses

quiz.q: Approximately how much does Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generate annually?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generates over $60 billion annually from skiing, hiking, mountain biking and other activities—making outdoor recreation a major driver of the state's economy and politics around climate and public lands.

laws.title: Greenhouse Gas Pollution Reduction Roadmap
laws.subtitle: 50% Emissions Cut by 2030
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's HB 21-1266 sets a target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions 50% below 2005 levels by 2030 and 90% by 2050. The state Air Quality Control Commission has authority to adopt sector-specific rules for transportation, buildings, and industry. Colorado has particular focus on oil and gas methane regulation as the state is a major natural gas producer, with SB 181 giving local governments authority to regulate oil and gas operations based on community health.
laws.penalty: Air quality violations: fines up to $15,000 per day; repeat violations escalate
exceptions: Agricultural emissions under separate framework
Small businesses under threshold levels

laws.title: Colorado Fentanyl Accountability and Prevention Act
laws.subtitle: Balancing Treatment and Enforcement
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Fentanyl Accountability and Prevention Act (2022) made possession of 1 gram or more of fentanyl a felony — responding to public pressure after Colorado had decriminalized drug possession. The law creates a middle path: a 'deflection fund' connects people arrested for drug possession to treatment rather than prosecution for first and second offenses. Colorado, which had decriminalized small drug amounts, faced public backlash over visible drug use after fentanyl contaminated the illicit drug supply. The law balances treatment approaches with enforcement for larger quantities.
laws.penalty: 1+ gram fentanyl possession: felony with up to 3 years; distribution: up to 16 years
exceptions: First and second possession offenses deflected to treatment
Medical fentanyl under valid prescription

laws.title: Colorado FAMLI — Paid Family and Medical Leave
laws.subtitle: State-Run Paid Leave Insurance
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) program, launched in 2024, provides up to 12 weeks of paid leave (16 weeks for complications of pregnancy) for bonding with a new child, caring for a family member, or managing a personal serious health condition. Workers receive up to 90% of wages (capped) funded by a 0.9% payroll premium split employer-employee. Colorado joined a growing number of states creating paid leave programs as federal legislation repeatedly failed. Workers have job protection during FAMLI leave.
laws.penalty: Employer retaliation for FAMLI leave: civil liability; failure to collect and remit premiums: financial penalties
exceptions: Employers with under 10 employees don't pay employer share (workers still covered)
Federal employees under separate federal FMLA

laws.title: Colorado Universal Preschool Program
laws.subtitle: Free Preschool for 4-Year-Olds
laws.fullDescription: Colorado launched a universal preschool program in 2023, providing 10-15 hours of free preschool weekly to all 4-year-olds — the first state to offer truly universal preschool access. Funded by a tobacco and nicotine tax increase, Colorado's program aims to close early childhood learning gaps and address childcare affordability. Colorado also has the Colorado Opportunity Fund for higher education, and has been expanding career and technical education. Colorado's school funding has historically been among the lowest per-pupil in the US, creating ongoing equity debates.
laws.penalty: Provider licensing required; child welfare standards enforced; funding accountability mechanisms
exceptions: Private preschool providers can participate as contractors
Children with disabilities may receive more hours

laws.title: Immigrant Rights Laws
laws.subtitle: Colorado's in-state tuition and sanctuary protections
laws.fullDescription: Colorado provides in-state tuition to undocumented students who graduated from Colorado high schools (Colorado ASSET Act, 2013). The state prohibits local law enforcement from detaining individuals based solely on immigration status (HB 1124, 2019). Colorado Driver's License Program extends licenses to residents regardless of immigration status. Colorado also created the Immigrant Assistance Program providing legal counsel. The state has an estimated 175,000 undocumented immigrants, significant in agricultural and construction sectors.
laws.penalty: Local law enforcement detaining individuals on immigration status alone violates state law; employers who use E-Verify to discriminate against authorized workers face state penalties
exceptions: Law enforcement may cooperate with federal immigration authorities regarding serious criminal offenders
Individuals convicted of certain crimes remain subject to standard immigration enforcement

quiz.q: Colorado's ASSET Act (2013) extended what benefit to undocumented students who graduated from Colorado high schools?
quiz.explanation: The Colorado ASSET Act allows undocumented students who attended and graduated from Colorado high schools to pay in-state tuition rates at public colleges and universities, rather than the higher out-of-state or international student rates.

laws.title: Amendment 64: First Legal Recreational Cannabis
laws.subtitle: Colorado's pioneering cannabis legalization
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Amendment 64 (2012) was the world's first modern law legalizing recreational cannabis at the state level — a landmark moment in drug policy. Colorado's regulated cannabis market has generated $10+ billion in sales and $1.6+ billion in tax revenue since 2014. The tax revenues fund education and public health. Colorado has struggled with youth access, drugged driving enforcement (no clear blood-THC standard), and the persistent black market. Colorado also decriminalized small amounts of psychedelics (psilocybin, MDMA) through Proposition 122 (2022).
laws.penalty: Cannabis possession over 2 oz: petty offense ($100 fine); over 6 oz: misdemeanor; unlicensed sales: felony; DUI cannabis: same as alcohol DUI; possession of hard drugs: misdemeanor (decriminalized under 4g for personal use since 2019 reform)
exceptions: Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz cannabis in public, up to 2 oz at home
Home cultivation up to 6 plants (3 mature)
Proposition 122 created regulated psilocybin healing centers
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Amendment 64 and Retail Cannabis Regulations

quiz.q: Colorado's Amendment 64 (2012) was the first law in the modern era to do what?
options: Legalize recreational cannabis at the state level worldwide
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Amendment 64 was the world's first modern state or national law to legalize recreational cannabis — passing simultaneously with Washington State's Initiative 502 on November 6, 2012, though Colorado's retail stores opened first on January 1, 2014.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Rights and Masterpiece Cakeshop
laws.subtitle: Colorado's LGBTQ+ framework and national legal battles
laws.fullDescription: Colorado has strong LGBTQ+ protections through its Anti-Discrimination Act (CADA), covering sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing, and public accommodations. Colorado legalized same-sex civil unions (2013) and was one of the first states to have marriage equality extended by federal court before the Supreme Court decision. Colorado became the center of a major national LGBTQ+ rights debate through Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission (2018) — the Supreme Court ruled narrowly for the baker but did not resolve the broader religious exemption question.
laws.penalty: Sexual orientation/gender identity discrimination: civil liability up to $15,000 per violation for repeat offenders; hate crimes: felony with sentence enhancement; misgendering transgender employees after being corrected: may constitute workplace harassment
exceptions: Religious organizations have some exemptions from employment non-discrimination for religious duties
The Masterpiece Cakeshop case left the religious exemption question partially unresolved
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act and Civil Rights Division

quiz.q: Colorado's Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission (2018) involved a baker who refused service to a same-sex couple based on what grounds?
options: Freedom of speech (artistic expression) and religious freedom
quiz.explanation: Jack Phillips of Masterpiece Cakeshop refused to bake a wedding cake for a same-sex couple citing his Christian religious beliefs and arguing that custom cake design is artistic expression protected by free speech. The Supreme Court ruled 7-2 for the baker on narrow grounds (hostile treatment by the Civil Rights Commission) without resolving the broader religious exemption question.

laws.title: Shield Law and Transparency Culture
laws.subtitle: Colorado has a strong tradition of press freedom with reporter shield protections
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's reporter privilege (CRS 13-90-119) protects journalists from compelled disclosure of sources or unpublished information. The privilege is qualified but provides substantial protection. Colorado's Open Records Act (CORA) provides public access to government records. Colorado has a vibrant local journalism scene including significant digital outlets. Denver Post and Colorado Public Radio serve as major outlets. Colorado courts have applied the reporter privilege broadly. The state has an anti-SLAPP statute protecting journalists and public speakers from meritless litigation.
laws.penalty: Journalists have qualified privilege; SLAPP suits can be dismissed with fee awards
exceptions: The privilege can be overcome upon showing the information is relevant, essential, and unavailable elsewhere

quiz.q: What does Colorado's Open Records Act (CORA) provide in relation to press freedom?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Open Records Act (CORA) provides public access to government records, a key component of press freedom that allows journalists to obtain documents for investigative reporting.

laws.title: Colorado Privacy Act and AI Regulation
laws.subtitle: Colorado has comprehensive privacy legislation and was first state to regulate AI decision-making
laws.fullDescription: Colorado passed the Colorado Privacy Act (CPA, 2021), providing consumer data rights including access, deletion, and opt-out from targeted advertising. Colorado also passed SB 205 (2024), the first US state law specifically regulating AI systems used in consequential decisions (employment, housing, credit) — requiring impact assessments and transparency. Colorado's approach represents a comprehensive tech regulation framework that addresses both privacy and AI fairness. The CPA went into effect July 1, 2023. Colorado's Consumer Protection Section enforces digital consumer rights.
laws.penalty: CPA violations: civil penalties enforceable by AG; SB 205 AI provisions: enforcement by AG
exceptions: Small businesses and nonprofits have some exemptions under CPA

quiz.q: What historic AI regulation did Colorado enact in 2024?
options: The first US state law regulating AI systems in consequential decisions
A mandatory AI content labeling law
An AI licensing requirement for companies
quiz.explanation: Colorado's SB 205 (2024) was the first US state law specifically regulating AI systems used in consequential decisions affecting employment, housing, and credit — requiring impact assessments and transparency measures, a landmark in AI governance.

laws.title: Colorado Digital Token Act and Financial Innovation
laws.subtitle: Colorado created a framework for digital tokens and blockchain financial applications
laws.fullDescription: Colorado passed the Colorado Digital Token Act (2019) and has been developing fintech-friendly financial regulation. Colorado's Division of Banking regulates state-chartered banks. Colorado's Division of Securities oversees investment products including digital assets. Colorado allows state income taxes to be paid in cryptocurrency (since 2022). Colorado has a growing fintech startup ecosystem in Denver and Boulder. Colorado's approach to digital assets has been more permissive than many states, positioning it as a financial innovation hub. The state has also focused on cannabis banking, given its legal marijuana industry needing banking services.
laws.penalty: Division of Banking and Securities enforcement; unlicensed financial services face civil and criminal penalties
exceptions: Colorado's Digital Token Act provides exemptions from securities laws for utility tokens

quiz.q: What unusual payment option did Colorado allow for state income taxes starting in 2022?
quiz.explanation: Colorado began accepting cryptocurrency for state income tax payments in 2022, becoming one of the first US states to do so — a symbolically significant step toward mainstream government acceptance of digital assets, processed through a third-party payment processor.

laws.title: Colorado Cottage Foods Act & Farm-to-Table Rules
laws.subtitle: Colorado has progressive cottage food laws supporting local food entrepreneurs
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Cottage Foods Act allows home food producers to sell a wide range of non-hazardous foods directly to consumers without commercial kitchen licensing, up to $50,000 annually. Colorado expanded the law in 2022 to allow online sales with in-person pickup and deliveries within certain distance limits. The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE) regulates food establishments statewide. Colorado has unique rules for its growing cannabis edibles market — the Marijuana Enforcement Division sets strict safety, labeling, and THC-content rules for edible cannabis products. Colorado's farm-to-school and farm-to-restaurant programs have driven specific local food safety standards to facilitate direct producer-institution sales.
laws.penalty: Cottage food violations: complaints can trigger CDPHE investigation; commercial food license violations: fines up to $1,000 per day; cannabis edible violations: product recall and license suspension
exceptions: Cottage food producers exempt from commercial licensing up to annual limits
Farm-to-school programs have modified liability frameworks
Specialty food producers at licensed farmers markets have exemptions

quiz.q: What unique food category does Colorado regulate separately through its Marijuana Enforcement Division?
options: Fermented beverages beyond standard alcohol rules
quiz.explanation: Colorado, as one of the first states to legalize recreational cannabis (Amendment 64 in 2012), developed comprehensive food safety rules for cannabis-infused edibles through its Marijuana Enforcement Division — covering THC content limits, child-resistant packaging, and distinct product labeling.

laws.title: Colorado Animal Cruelty and Pet Animal Care Laws
laws.subtitle: Colorado bans breed-specific legislation at state level
laws.fullDescription: Colorado Revised Statutes Title 18-9-202 makes animal cruelty a class 1 misdemeanor (neglect/abandonment) or class 6 felony (aggravated cruelty). Colorado's Pet Animal Care and Facilities Act (PACFA) regulates breeding facilities, pet stores, and animal shelters. In 2023, Colorado passed SB 23-241 banning the retail sale of dogs and cats from commercial breeders in pet stores. Colorado also preempts local breed-specific legislation (BSL) — municipalities may not ban specific dog breeds. Statewide, dogfighting is a felony, and animal hoarding is addressed under cruelty statutes. Colorado has a progressive stance on wolf reintroduction (Proposition 114, 2020), balancing wildlife and livestock interests.
laws.penalty: Class 1 misdemeanor: up to 364 days; class 6 felony cruelty: 1–18 months; aggravated cruelty: class 5 felony up to 3 years + up to $100,000 fine
exceptions: Livestock practices including branding, dehorning, ear tagging
Hunting, trapping, fishing with valid Colorado license
Scientific research with IACUC approval

quiz.q: What does Colorado's state law say about breed-specific legislation (BSL) like pit bull bans?
options: Colorado preempts local BSL — cities cannot ban specific breeds
quiz.explanation: Colorado state law preempts breed-specific legislation, meaning municipalities cannot ban or restrict ownership of specific dog breeds. This makes Colorado one of the most permissive states for dog breed ownership rights.

laws.title: Colorado Equitable Distribution and Parental Responsibility
laws.subtitle: Colorado uses Allocation of Parental Responsibilities rather than custody
laws.fullDescription: Colorado uses equitable distribution for property division and calls child arrangements 'Allocation of Parental Responsibilities' (APR) rather than custody — a modern terminology reflecting child-centered thinking. Colorado courts consider numerous factors for APR: each parent's fitness, child's adjustment to home/school/community, each parent's willingness to encourage relationships with the other parent, and any history of domestic violence. Colorado's Uniform Dissolution of Marriage Act requires a 91-day waiting period from service of divorce papers. Colorado was the first state to recognize same-sex civil unions (2013) before marriage equality. Colorado also has specific laws protecting victims of domestic violence within family court proceedings.
laws.penalty: Civil enforcement; contempt: fines and imprisonment; child support: administrative enforcement, licence suspension, credit reporting, passport denial
exceptions: Premarital agreements
Separate property retained
Mediation required before contested hearings in many counties
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Revised Statutes Title 14 — Domestic Matters

quiz.q: What terminology does Colorado use instead of 'custody' in child arrangements?
options: Allocation of Parental Responsibilities (APR) — child-centered modern terminology
quiz.explanation: Colorado uses 'Allocation of Parental Responsibilities' (APR) instead of the traditional 'custody' terminology — a modern, child-centered framing that focuses on the responsibilities each parent has for the child rather than treating the child as property to be 'won' in a custody dispute.

laws.title: Colorado Property Rights & Housing Legislation
laws.subtitle: 2023 tenant protections and zoning reform
laws.fullDescription: Colorado reversed its ban on local rent control with SB 23-184 (2023), allowing local governments to enact rent stabilization. Denver and other cities began exploring rent-stabilization measures. The state also passed HB 24-1098 requiring just cause for evictions statewide after the initial lease term. Additionally, HB 24-1313 enabled transit-oriented communities by requiring denser zoning near transit stations, addressing the housing shortage.
laws.penalty: Wrongful eviction: actual damages and attorney fees; rent stabilization enforcement by local jurisdiction
exceptions: Just cause applies after initial lease term only
Local governments may set rent stabilization rules
laws.source: SB 23-184; HB 24-1098; Colo. Rev. Stat. Sec. 38-12

quiz.q: What did Colorado SB 23-184 (2023) reverse regarding rent control?
options: It reversed the ban on local rent control
It set a statewide rent cap
quiz.explanation: SB 23-184 reversed Colorado's previous preemption of local rent control, allowing municipalities to enact their own rent stabilization ordinances for the first time since the 1980s ban.

laws.title: Colorado Privacy Act & Consumer Protection Laws
laws.subtitle: 2023 comprehensive privacy law and consumer rights
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Privacy Act (CPA, effective July 2023) gives residents rights to access, correct, delete, and opt out of the processing of their personal data for targeted advertising and profiling. It applies to controllers processing data of 100,000+ Colorado consumers annually. The Colorado Consumer Protection Act (CRS § 6-1-105) prohibits deceptive trade practices. Colorado has a distinctive 'Cooling-Off' rule requiring a 3-business-day cancellation right for door-to-door sales over $25. The Colorado AG enforces both laws. Colorado also has specific auto dealer fraud protections and the Uniform Consumer Credit Code governing credit transactions.
laws.penalty: CPA violation: AG enforcement, up to $20,000 per violation; CCPA deceptive practices: actual damages + attorney fees
exceptions: CPA applies to controllers processing 100,000+ Colorado consumers' data
3-day cooling-off period for door-to-door sales over $25

quiz.q: What right does Colorado's Privacy Act give consumers regarding targeted advertising?
options: The right to be paid for data use
The right to opt out of processing their data for targeted advertising
The right to sue advertisers directly
The right to delete all online ads
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Privacy Act (2023) gives residents the right to opt out of the processing of their personal data for targeted advertising, profiling, and sale — one of the key consumer controls in the growing wave of state comprehensive privacy laws.

laws.title: Amendment 64 — First Recreational Cannabis Market (2012)
laws.subtitle: Colorado — One of first states to legalize
laws.fullDescription: Colorado was one of the first two states to legalize recreational cannabis in November 2012. Adults 21+ may possess up to 1 oz in public, grow up to 3 plants at home (6 per household), and purchase from licensed retailers. Colorado's regulated market launched January 2014. Colorado collected over $1.6 billion in cannabis taxes by 2023.
laws.penalty: Possession over 1 oz (under 2 oz): class 2 petty offense. Over 6 oz: class 3 felony.
exceptions: Home cultivation of 3 plants allowed (6 per household)
Medical patients may possess more
Local jurisdictions may ban retail sales

quiz.q: How many cannabis plants may a Colorado adult grow at home?
quiz.explanation: Colorado allows adults 21+ to cultivate up to 3 plants per adult, with a maximum of 6 plants per household.

laws.title: Colorado River Compact & Water Rights Crisis
laws.subtitle: 1922 Compact — Prior appropriation water law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado was a signatory to the 1922 Colorado River Compact allocating river water. The river has been over-allocated for decades. Drought and climate change triggered federal mandatory cuts. Lake Mead and Lake Powell hit historic lows. Colorado uses prior appropriation ('first in time, first in right') water law.
laws.penalty: Violating water rights: civil enforcement, loss of water rights.
exceptions: Senior water rights holders protected by prior appropriation
Agricultural uses historically get priority over municipal
Tribal water rights claims ongoing

quiz.q: How is water distributed in Colorado under prior appropriation?
options: First in time, first in right — older rights take priority
quiz.explanation: Colorado uses prior appropriation: 'first in time, first in right.' Older water rights have priority during shortages — junior rights holders face cuts first during drought.

laws.title: Red Flag Law — ERPO (2019)
laws.subtitle: Colorado ERPO — Extreme Risk Protection Orders
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Extreme Risk Protection Order law (2019) allows family members, household members, or law enforcement to petition courts to temporarily remove firearms from individuals who pose a significant risk. The order lasts up to 364 days. Colorado passed the law after the 2019 STEM School Highlands Ranch shooting.
laws.penalty: Violating an ERPO: class 2 misdemeanor. Filing false ERPO petition: class 2 misdemeanor.
exceptions: Due process: respondent can challenge at hearing
Firearms returned after order expires or is dismissed
Law enforcement must store confiscated firearms

quiz.q: Who can petition for an Extreme Risk Protection Order (ERPO) in Colorado?
options: Law enforcement, family members, or household members
quiz.explanation: In Colorado, ERPOs can be filed by law enforcement, family members, or household members who believe someone poses a significant risk of harm with a firearm.

laws.title: Non-Compete Law Reform (2022) — HB 22-1317
laws.subtitle: Colorado HB 1317 — Major limits on non-competes
laws.fullDescription: Colorado dramatically reformed non-compete law in 2022. Non-compete agreements are only enforceable for employees earning more than $123,750/year (2024 threshold, CPI-adjusted) and only to protect trade secrets. Non-solicitation agreements have a lower threshold. Prior non-compliant agreements are void.
laws.penalty: Unenforceable non-competes: void. Employer using void non-compete to harm employee: attorney's fees and damages.
exceptions: Sale of business non-competes still permitted
Executives may have broader agreements
Certain licensed professions have separate rules

quiz.q: What is the minimum salary for a non-compete to be enforceable in Colorado (2024)?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's HB 22-1317 limits non-compete agreements to employees earning above ~$123,750/year. Non-competes for lower-paid workers are void and unenforceable.

laws.title: FAMLI — Paid Family & Medical Leave (2024)
laws.subtitle: Colorado FAMLI — 12 weeks paid leave
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) program began paying benefits in January 2024. Employees receive up to 12 weeks (up to 16 for pregnancy complications) of paid leave at up to 90% of wages (capped at $1,100/week). Funded by employee and employer payroll contributions.
laws.penalty: Employer interference with FAMLI rights: penalties, back pay.
exceptions: Self-employed workers may opt in voluntarily
Local governments may opt out
Small employers (under 10) exempt from employer premium

quiz.q: When did Colorado's FAMLI paid leave program begin paying benefits?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's FAMLI program began collecting premiums in 2023 and started paying benefits in January 2024, providing up to 12 weeks of paid family or medical leave.

laws.title: Climate Action Plan — 50% Emissions Cut by 2030
laws.subtitle: Colorado SB 19-096 — Net zero by 2050
laws.fullDescription: Colorado set mandatory greenhouse gas reduction goals: 50% below 2005 levels by 2030, and net zero by 2050. Colorado has been severely impacted by wildfires, drought, and shifting snowpack. CDPHE and AQCC implement sector-specific rules for oil & gas, transportation, and buildings.
laws.penalty: Air quality violations: CDPHE fines, compliance orders.
exceptions: Agricultural operations have modified rules
Small businesses get compliance assistance
Emergency exemptions for grid reliability
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Dept. of Public Health & Environment

quiz.q: By what percentage must Colorado reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 2030?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's SB 19-096 requires a 50% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (compared to 2005 levels), with net zero by 2050.

laws.title: TABOR — Taxpayer's Bill of Rights
laws.subtitle: Colorado Constitution Art. X §20 — Voter approval for taxes
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's TABOR (1992) requires voter approval for all tax increases and limits government revenue growth to inflation plus population growth. Excess revenue must be refunded to taxpayers. TABOR has significantly constrained Colorado's state and local budgets. TABOR is uniquely Colorado.
laws.penalty: Government spending in excess of TABOR limits: refunds required, legal challenges.
exceptions: Voter approval allows tax increases beyond limits
Emergency provisions in some cases
Federal funding not subject to TABOR

quiz.q: What does Colorado's TABOR require for any state or local tax increase?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's TABOR (Taxpayer's Bill of Rights) requires voter approval for all tax increases and limits government revenue growth — a unique constitutional provision.

laws.title: ADU Rights — HB 24-1152 (2024)
laws.subtitle: Colorado requires municipalities to allow ADUs
laws.fullDescription: Colorado passed HB 24-1152 in 2024 requiring municipalities to allow at least one ADU per single-family lot, preempting local zoning bans. ADUs (granny flats, garage apartments) increase housing supply. Colorado faces a significant housing shortage. Cities must update zoning codes by 2027.
laws.penalty: Non-compliant cities: state enforcement and potential loss of state funding.
exceptions: Owner-occupancy requirements may still apply in some cases
Design standards that aren't overly restrictive may remain
Areas without adequate infrastructure may petition for extensions

quiz.q: What housing type did Colorado's 2024 HB 24-1152 require municipalities to permit?
options: ADUs (Accessory Dwelling Units) on single-family lots
quiz.explanation: Colorado's HB 24-1152 requires all municipalities to allow at least one ADU per single-family lot, overriding local zoning bans to address the state's housing shortage.

laws.title: All-Mail Voting — Colorado's Model System
laws.subtitle: Colorado Voter Access and Modernized Elections Act
laws.fullDescription: Colorado pioneered all-mail voting — every registered voter automatically receives a ballot by mail before each election. Ballots can be returned by mail or dropped at drop boxes. Colorado consistently has among the highest voter turnout in the US. The system has been studied as a national model.
laws.penalty: Voter fraud: class 5 felony.
exceptions: Voters may opt to always vote in person
Overseas and military voters use UOCAVA rules
Same-day registration available at polling locations

quiz.q: What does Colorado do with all registered voters before each election?
quiz.explanation: Colorado automatically mails a ballot to every registered voter before each election, producing some of the nation's highest voter turnout rates.

laws.title: Colorado Privacy Act — Consumer Data Rights (2023)
laws.subtitle: Colorado Privacy Act (CPA)
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Privacy Act (2021, effective 2023) gives residents rights over personal data: access, correct, delete, and opt out of sale of data and targeted advertising. Applies to companies processing data of 100,000+ Colorado consumers, or 25,000+ if 25%+ of revenue from data sales. AG enforces.
laws.penalty: CPA violations: civil penalties up to $20,000/violation.
exceptions: HIPAA-regulated health data exempt
GLBA financial data exempt
Employee data has separate rules

quiz.q: What can Coloradans opt out of under the Colorado Privacy Act?
options: Opting out of all data collection
Opting out of sale of data and targeted advertising
Opting out of government data use
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Privacy Act grants consumers the right to opt out of the sale of their personal data and its use for targeted advertising.

laws.title: Chain Laws — Traction and Chain Requirements
laws.subtitle: Colorado CDR 8 CCR 1507-22 — Winter traction law
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's chain law applies on mountain highways when conditions are dangerous. Traction tires (winter tires meeting specific ratings) are required when the law is activated. Chains are required on commercial vehicles. Passenger vehicles without adequate tires must carry chains.
laws.penalty: Violating traction law: $130 fine. Causing accident due to improper tires: up to $650 fine.
exceptions: 4WD/AWD vehicles with adequate tires may substitute for some requirements
Emergency vehicles exempt
Vehicles with chains are always compliant

quiz.q: Under Colorado's chain law, which vehicles must ALWAYS have chains (not just traction tires)?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's chain law requires commercial vehicles to have actual chains in chain law conditions — traction tires alone are not sufficient for commercial trucks.

laws.title: Colorado Option — Public Health Insurance (2021)
laws.subtitle: SB 21-175 — Publicly developed plan through carriers
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's 'Option' (2021) is a unique public health insurance option offered through private carriers on Connect for Health Colorado. Carriers must offer standardized Colorado Option plans meeting state cost reduction targets (15% below 2021 premiums by 2025). If carriers don't meet targets, the state can require it.
laws.penalty: Carriers not meeting Option cost targets face mandated participation.
exceptions: Small group and individual markets covered
Large employer plans not required
Rural areas have targeted support

quiz.q: What makes Colorado's 'Option' health insurance unique nationally?
options: Private carriers offer it but must meet state cost reduction targets
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Option is offered through private carriers (not a government plan) but requires those carriers to meet state-mandated cost reduction targets — a hybrid approach unique among US states.

laws.title: Great Outdoors Colorado — Conservation Easements
laws.subtitle: Colorado GOCO — Lottery-funded conservation
laws.fullDescription: Colorado has protected over 3.3 million acres through conservation easements and Great Outdoors Colorado (GOCO) funded by Lottery proceeds. Conservation easements allow landowners to permanently restrict development in exchange for tax benefits. GOCO has invested $1.3 billion in parks, trails, and wildlife habitat since 1994.
laws.penalty: Violations of conservation easement terms: court enforcement, loss of tax benefits.
exceptions: Agricultural use typically allowed under conservation easements
Public access not always required — private conservation easements exist
Emergency access for utilities may be permitted

quiz.q: What funds Colorado's Great Outdoors Colorado (GOCO) conservation program?
quiz.explanation: Great Outdoors Colorado (GOCO) is funded by a portion of Colorado Lottery proceeds, established by constitutional amendment in 1992.

laws.title: Equal Pay for Equal Work Act — Salary Transparency (2021)
laws.subtitle: Colorado HB 19-085 — Job posting salary requirements
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (2021) requires employers to include salary ranges AND qualifications in all job postings. Colorado was among the first states with this requirement. The law prohibits wage secrecy policies. Many national companies initially excluded Colorado applicants in remote job postings.
laws.penalty: Violations: civil action, back pay, attorney's fees, fines up to $10,000.
exceptions: Employers with no Colorado employees may have different obligations
Contract workers have modified rules
Commission structures must disclose total compensation range
laws.sourceLabel: Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act

quiz.q: What must Colorado employers include in job postings under the Equal Pay for Equal Work Act?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's Equal Pay for Equal Work Act requires all job postings to include the salary range and qualifications — one of the first state salary transparency laws nationally.

laws.title: Natural Medicine Decriminalization — Prop 122 (2022)
laws.subtitle: Colorado Prop 122 — Psychedelics healing act
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters approved Proposition 122 in 2022, decriminalizing personal possession and use of psilocybin mushrooms, DMT, mescaline, ibogaine, and psilocyn for adults 21+. Licensed healing centers may facilitate guided psychedelic experiences. Colorado became the second state (after Oregon) to create a regulated psilocybin framework.
laws.penalty: Commercial sale without license remains illegal. Possession beyond allowed amounts still criminal.
exceptions: Healing centers require licenses
No smoking or vaping of natural medicines in public
Cannot give to minors

quiz.q: Which state first created a regulated psilocybin healing framework before Colorado?
quiz.explanation: Oregon passed Measure 109 in 2020, creating the nation's first regulated psilocybin therapy program. Colorado's Proposition 122 (2022) was the second.

laws.title: E-Bike Rebate Program — Up to $1,500
laws.subtitle: Colorado HB 22-1289 — E-bike rebates
laws.fullDescription: Colorado created an innovative e-bike rebate program in 2022, offering up to $1,500 ($450 for lower incomes) for e-bike purchases to reduce vehicle trips. Colorado classifies e-bikes in three classes. Class 1 and 2 are allowed on most bike paths; Class 3 on roads.
laws.penalty: Riding e-bikes in prohibited areas: traffic fines.
exceptions: Class 3 e-bikes restricted to roads and designated paths
Age restrictions: riders under 16 cannot ride Class 3
E-bikes may not be modified beyond class speed limits

quiz.q: What is the maximum rebate amount for standard e-bike purchases under Colorado's program?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's e-bike rebate program offers up to $1,500 for standard e-bike purchases ($450 for lower-income residents) to reduce car trips.

laws.title: Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act (CADA)
laws.subtitle: Colorado Revised Statutes §24-34-301
laws.fullDescription: Colorado's Anti-Discrimination Act was one of the first to add sexual orientation and gender identity as protected classes (sexual orientation added 1990, gender identity 2007). The Colorado Civil Rights Division enforces. In 2023, the US Supreme Court addressed CADA in 303 Creative v. Elenis.
laws.penalty: Discrimination violations: Colorado Civil Rights Commission enforcement, civil lawsuits, back pay.
exceptions: Religious organizations have hiring exemptions
Bona fide occupational qualifications
Religious expression concerns addressed under 303 Creative

quiz.q: When did Colorado add sexual orientation to its Anti-Discrimination Act?
quiz.explanation: Colorado added sexual orientation to its Anti-Discrimination Act in 1990, making it an early leader in LGBTQ+ employment and housing protections.

laws.title: Agricultural Water Transfers — Buy and Dry Protections
laws.subtitle: Colorado water law — Protecting agricultural communities
laws.fullDescription: Colorado has seen 'buy and dry' water transfers where cities buy agricultural water rights, drying up farms. Colorado's HB 22-1233 created new requirements for large water transfers, requiring water courts to consider impacts on agricultural communities. Colorado is developing water-sharing arrangements.
laws.penalty: Water transfers without proper court approval: civil injunction, loss of transfer approval.
exceptions: Dry year leasing (temporary transfers) allowed with fewer restrictions
Fallowing programs allow partial year transfers
Some agricultural-to-municipal transfers pre-approved

quiz.q: What is 'buy and dry' in Colorado water law?
options: Agricultural water rights purchased by cities, permanently drying up farmland
Buying water from the federal government
quiz.explanation: 'Buy and dry' refers to municipalities purchasing agricultural water rights and transferring them to urban use, permanently drying up the farmland. Colorado enacted protections for affected communities.

laws.title: Independent Redistricting Commissions — Colorado
laws.subtitle: Colorado Amendments Y and Z (2018)
laws.fullDescription: Colorado voters created independent redistricting commissions in 2018 (Amendments Y and Z) for congressional and legislative districts. The 12-member commissions (4 Republicans, 4 Democrats, 4 unaffiliated) draw maps with transparency requirements. Approved by the Colorado Supreme Court.
laws.penalty: Legislative interference: potential constitutional violation.
exceptions: Commission decisions subject to Colorado Supreme Court review
VRA compliance required
Commission itself not immune from lawsuits challenging maps

quiz.q: How many members serve on Colorado's independent redistricting commissions?
quiz.explanation: Colorado's independent redistricting commissions have 12 members: 4 Republicans, 4 Democrats, and 4 unaffiliated voters, selected through an application and screening process.

laws.title: 42% Public Land — Recreation Economy
laws.subtitle: Colorado public lands — $62 billion recreation economy
laws.fullDescription: About 42% of Colorado is public land — National Forests, BLM land, national parks, and state parks. Colorado's outdoor recreation economy generates $62 billion annually and employs 229,000 people. 'Leave No Trace' principles are embedded in state messaging. Colorado's ski industry operates on National Forest land under federal permits.
laws.penalty: Criminal trespass on private land: class 1 petty offense ($100) to class 5 felony.
exceptions: Public lands freely accessible to all
Established trail easements across private land are legal
Hunting with landowner permission on private land permitted

quiz.q: Approximately what percentage of Colorado is public land?
quiz.explanation: About 42% of Colorado is public land — including National Forests, BLM land, National Parks, and state parks.
